When `TrailingSlash` is `Never`, it answers one with a trailing slash in the same way, whether or not `RedirectLiteralCase` is on ([One URL per page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/routing.md#one-url-per-page)). Call it before authentication and before `UseOutputCache()`, which then never stores a spelling these settings redirect: another case of a literal segment, and under `Never` a trailing slash. A server action that fails without JavaScript renders its form's page by running the pipeline again from here, so middleware registered before `UseNetjes()` does not run for that render. In production it reads the client build's manifest, and throws when it is missing, saying what to run: an app that does not catch it logs that in one line and exits with code 1. It also stops an app with Next.js pages router files in a `pages/` folder, naming the `app/` file to move each one to, and the API routes in `pages/api/` to map as minimal API endpoints ([Routing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/routing.md#what-is-not-there)).

### MapPages

```csharp
public static IEndpointConventionBuilder MapPages(this IEndpointRouteBuilder endpoints)
```

Maps every page file that has no `MapPageLoader`, a lowest-priority fallback that renders the not-found page, the image endpoint (`/_netjes/image`, for `GET` and `HEAD`), the antiforgery token endpoint (`/_netjes/antiforgery`, for `GET` only), and with `CollectWebVitals` the vitals endpoint (`/_netjes/vitals`). Conventions on the result, such as `RequireAuthorization()` or `CachePage(...)`, apply to all the file pages. It reads the routes as the app starts, so files in `app/` that break the file conventions stop the app there ([Route errors](#route-errors)).

### AddNetjes (health checks)

```csharp
public static IHealthChecksBuilder AddNetjes(this IHealthChecksBuilder builder)
```

Adds a health check named `netjes` for the Node processes: Healthy when all are ready, Degraded while some restart, Unhealthy when none is ready. A process counts as restarting from the moment it is taken out: when it exits, and in production also when it stops answering. See [deployment](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/deployment.md#health-checks).

### GetNetjesCommand

```csharp
public static string? GetNetjesCommand(this IHost host)
```

The `netjes` CLI command this run of the app is for (`generate`, `routes` or `export`), or `null` for an ordinary run. `generate` and `routes` answer no requests, so startup work they do not need can be skipped: `if (app.GetNetjesCommand() is null) await SeedAsync(app.Services);`. `export` renders every page, so it needs what the pages need.

## Pages and loaders

### MapPageLoader

```csharp
public static RouteHandlerBuilder MapPageLoader(this IEndpointRouteBuilder endpoints, string pattern, Delegate loader)
```

The C# loader of a page, in place of a server component or `getServerSideProps`. `pattern` is the page's URL in file syntax (`/blog/[slug]`) and must match a page file; otherwise it throws, naming the file it expected and the pages there are. The endpoint answers `GET` and `HEAD` at the page's URL, below the prefix of a route group it is mapped in (`app.MapGroup("/{tenant}")`), whose route parameters it binds as it binds the page's own. The delegate binds like a minimal API `GET` handler (route values, the query string, services, `HttpContext`, `ClaimsPrincipal`, `CancellationToken`, no request body) and returns a `PageResult` or `PageResult<T>`; its return type names the props type for the generated TypeScript. A parameter minimal APIs cannot bind, such as a complex type that is not a registered service and has no `[AsParameters]`, throws here, naming the page, the parameter and the fixes, and so does one that reads the request body (`[FromBody]`, `[FromForm]`, `IFormFile`, `IFormFileCollection`, `IFormCollection`), which a navigation does not have, or an `IEnumerable<int>`, which minimal APIs would take from services and not from the query string, as `int[]` is, or a type that adds accepts metadata (`IAcceptsMetadata`) for itself, with which routing would match the page only for requests with that Content-Type and no navigation would reach it ([binding](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/data-loading.md#binding)). The result is a `RouteHandlerBuilder`, so `RequireAuthorization()`, `CachePage()`, `CacheOutput()`, filters and metadata work as on any endpoint, except accepts metadata (`.Accepts<T>()`), which would keep navigations from the page in the same way. Conventions of layout loaders above the page apply to it too. See [data loading](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/data-loading.md).

### MapLayoutLoader

```csharp
public static LayoutLoaderBuilder MapLayoutLoader(this IEndpointRouteBuilder endpoints, string segment, Delegate loader)
```

The C# loader of a `layout.tsx`: its props reach the layout component next to `children` and `params`. `segment` is the layout's URL (`/dashboard`, `/[team]`) or, when route groups share a URL, its folder (`app/(shop)`); it throws when no layout or several match. The loader binds like a minimal API `GET` handler, from the route values of the layout's own URL, the query string and services, with no inferred body; a parameter it cannot bind, such as a `[FromRoute]` naming a route value outside the layout's URL, a complex type that is not a registered service and does not bind itself, one that reads the request body (`[FromBody]`, `[FromForm]`, `IFormFile`, `IFormFileCollection`, `IFormCollection`), or an `IEnumerable<int>`, which minimal APIs would take from services, throws here, naming the layout ([what a layout loader binds](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/data-loading.md#what-a-layout-loader-binds)). It runs before the page renders, outermost layout first, and is skipped on client navigations while its route values and the user stay the same. `NotFound`, `Forbidden` and `Unauthorized` render the boundary above the layout; `Redirect` redirects the page. Conventions on the result, such as `RequireAuthorization()`, apply to every page below the layout. Access checks on route values deeper than the layout's URL belong in the page's loader. Mapping a second loader for one layout throws.

### LayoutLoaderBuilder

```csharp
public sealed class LayoutLoaderBuilder : IEndpointConventionBuilder
{
    public void Add(Action<EndpointBuilder> convention);
    public void Finally(Action<EndpointBuilder> finallyConvention);
}
```

What `MapLayoutLoader` returns. Each convention is applied to the layout loader and to every page endpoint below the layout, so `RequireAuthorization()` on it protects the whole section before any loader runs.

### MapPageAction

```csharp
public static RouteHandlerBuilder MapPageAction(this IEndpointRouteBuilder endpoints, string pattern, Delegate action)
```

A `POST` handler at a page's URL, for `<Form method="post">` on that page, with or without JavaScript. Bind fields with `[FromForm]`; a delegate minimal APIs cannot bind, such as one with two inferred bodies, throws here, naming the page ([page actions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/actions-and-forms.md#page-actions)), and so does a `[FromForm]` input with several public constructors or none, or an abstract or interface type, which form binding never builds. Return `Page.Redirect(...)` after a change, or `Page.Props(...)` (often `.WithStatus(422)`) to render the page again, with errors you put in the props. Before the delegate runs, the DataAnnotations of its inputs, and then `IValidatableObject`, are checked as for `MapAction`, with or without `AddValidation()`; a failure renders the page again from its loader with status 422, and the page reads the errors and the declared fields' values with `usePageActionState()` ([validation in page actions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/actions-and-forms.md#validation-in-page-actions)). An attribute that cannot be read throws here. A `[FromForm]` input is never `null` unless the parameter is declared nullable: a post with none of its fields gets an empty input, checked like any other. It always requires a valid antiforgery token, also when it binds no form fields, and a same-origin request, so `app.UseAntiforgery()` must be in the pipeline. `.DisableAntiforgery()` turns off both, for a form another site posts back. The server's request size limit applies, not `ActionBodySizeLimit`. A post from the client router whose response sets or deletes a cookie is marked `X-Netjes-Cookies: changed`. See [actions and forms](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/actions-and-forms.md).

### Page

```csharp
public static class Page
{
    public static PageResult<TProps> Props<TProps>(TProps props);
    public static PageResult<NoProps> Props();
    public static PageResult Render(string pattern, object? props = null);
    public static PageResult NotFound();
    public static PageResult Forbidden();
    public static PageResult Unauthorized();
    public static PageResult Redirect(string location, bool permanent = false);
    public static PageResult LocalRedirect(string location, bool permanent = false);
    public static bool IsLocalUrl(string? url);
    public static Deferred<T> Defer<T>(Task<T> task);
    public static Deferred<T> Defer<T>(Func<IServiceProvider, Task<T>> load);
}
```

Results for page loaders, layout loaders and page actions.

| Member | What it does |
|---|---|
| `Props(props)` | Render the endpoint's page with these props. The result is typed by them, so the loader's inferred return type names the props for the generated TypeScript and for tests (`result.Props`). Only in endpoints mapped with `MapPageLoader` or `MapPageAction`; it throws elsewhere. |
| `Props()` | The same without props (`{}`). |
| `Render(pattern, props)` | Render the page for `pattern` (`/blog/[slug]`) from any endpoint, such as a minimal API. |
| `NotFound()` | Render the nearest `not-found.tsx`, inside the layouts above it, else the root not-found page, with status 404. |
| `Forbidden()` | Render the nearest `forbidden.tsx`, else the error page, with status 403. |
| `Unauthorized()` | Render the nearest `unauthorized.tsx`, else the error page, with status 401. |
| `Redirect(location, permanent)` | Redirect: 307 (308 when `permanent`) for `GET` and `HEAD`, 303 after a `POST`. The client router follows it without a full page load. Accepts relative URLs and `http`/`https` URLs, and throws for any other scheme and for a `%` before the first `:` or `/`. |
| `LocalRedirect(location, permanent)` | Like `Redirect`, but throws unless `location` is a path on this site. Use it for URLs that come from the request, such as a `returnUrl`. |
| `IsLocalUrl(url)` | Whether `url` is a path on this site by ASP.NET Core's rules (`/path`, not `//host` or `/\host`), after dropping what browsers drop. Check a `returnUrl` with it and fall back instead of throwing. |
| `Defer(task)` | A prop that is still being computed: the page renders without waiting, and the task's result streams to it when it completes. Read it with `use()` inside a Suspense boundary. |
| `Defer(load)` | The same, with the work started once the page's payload is written, in a DI scope of its own: for work that needs scoped services such as a `DbContext`. |

See [rendering and streaming](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/rendering-and-streaming.md#slow-data-with-pagedefer) for `Defer`.

### PageResult

```csharp
public sealed class PageResult : IResult
{
    public PageResult WithStatus(int statusCode);
    public PageResult WithMetadata(PageMetadata metadata);
    public PageResult WithQuery(IReadOnlyList<object?> queryKey, object? data);
    public Task ExecuteAsync(HttpContext httpContext);
}
```

What the untyped `Page` methods return.

- `WithStatus(statusCode)` renders with another status, such as 422 when a page action renders the form again with errors.
- `WithMetadata(metadata)` sets the title, description, Open Graph and other head tags from C#, merged over the metadata the page and layout files export (layout title templates still apply), like `generateMetadata`. See [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/metadata.md).
- `WithQuery(queryKey, data)` seeds the page's TanStack Query cache: `useQuery` with that key renders `data` on the server and on the first render in the browser, without fetching. It is fetched again once stale (`staleTime`, one minute by default), and data the browser fetched more recently is kept. It throws for an empty key; chain it for several queries.

### PageResult&lt;TProps&gt;

```csharp
public sealed class PageResult<TProps> : IResult
{
    public TProps? Props { get; }
    public PageResult<TProps> WithStatus(int statusCode);
    public PageResult<TProps> WithQuery(IReadOnlyList<object?> queryKey, object? data);
    public PageResult<TProps> WithMetadata(PageMetadata metadata);
    public Task ExecuteAsync(HttpContext httpContext);
    public static implicit operator PageResult<TProps>(PageResult result);
}
```

What `Page.Props(props)` returns. Every untyped result converts to it, so one loader can return the page or `NotFound()`, `Redirect(...)` and the rest, and its inferred return type is still `PageResult<TProps>`. `Props` holds the props when the result renders the page, and is `null` for a redirect, not-found or status result.

### NoProps

```csharp
public sealed record NoProps;
```

The props type of `Page.Props()`, serialized as `{}`.

### Deferred&lt;T&gt;

```csharp
public sealed class Deferred<T>;
```

The type of a `Page.Defer` prop. Declare props with it (`Deferred<IReadOnlyList<Comment>> Comments`); the generated TypeScript types it as a `deferred()` schema. It serializes as a placeholder, and only inside page and layout props.

### Href

```csharp
[JsonConverter(typeof(HrefJsonConverter))]
public sealed class Href : IEquatable<Href>
{
    public Href(string url);
    public string Value { get; }
    public static bool TryCreate(string? url, out Href? href);
    public bool Equals(Href? other);
    public override string ToString();
    public static bool operator ==(Href? left, Href? right);
    public static bool operator !=(Href? left, Href? right);
    public static implicit operator string?(Href? href);
}

public sealed class HrefJsonConverter : JsonConverter<Href>;
```

A link in props, to one of the app's pages or to another site: a root-relative URL without the base path (`/blog/hello`, `/docs/guides/caching#keys`), a query or a fragment of the page on screen (`?page=2`, `#top`), or an `http:`, `https:`, `mailto:` or `tel:` URL. The generated TypeScript types a property of this type as the `Href` schema, which checks it against the app's pages where the props are parsed, so a component passes it to `<Link>` without `Href.parse` or a cast ([Links from C#](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/data-loading.md#links-from-c)). `Href?`, lists, dictionaries and `Deferred<Href>` are generated as `Href.nullable()`, `z.array(Href)`, `z.record(z.string(), Href)` and `deferred(Href)`.

- `new Href(url)` throws `ArgumentException` for a URL that starts with none of `/`, `?`, `#`, `http:`, `https:`, `mailto:` and `tel:` (the schemes in any case); starts with `//` or `/\`, which browsers read as another host; holds an ASCII control character, such as a tab or a newline, which browsers drop (`/\t/evil.example` goes to `evil.example`); or starts or ends with a space. It throws `ArgumentNullException` for `null`. `TryCreate` checks the same and returns `false`, with `href` set to `null`, where the constructor would throw.
- C# checks the shape of the URL, not whether it is a page: `/llms.txt` and a URL that already has the base path are valid here. Where the props are parsed, on the server and in the browser, a root-relative `Href` that no page serves fails the parse with `Invalid props: …` (`Invalid layout props: …` or `Invalid shared props: …` for those), which goes to the nearest error boundary. A server render answers that with status 500 only when the component that parses is outside every Suspense boundary; under one, such as a `loading.tsx`, the document goes out with the loader's status and that boundary's fallback, and the error page shows once the parse fails in the browser. Make an `Href` only of a URL the code knows to be a page; a link to an endpoint or a file stays a `string`.
- It has no base path: the client router adds the app's, as it does for every root-relative link. `LinkGenerator`'s overloads that take an `HttpContext` add the request's base path, so pass them `pathBase: PathString.Empty` for a URL that goes into an `Href`.
- JSON holds it as a plain string, in props and in any other JSON written with the app's options: the type names its converter, `HrefJsonConverter`, which is public so that a System.Text.Json source-generated context (`JsonSerializerContext`) in the app can create it too. Reading a string without that shape, or a number, an object or an array, throws `JsonException` (`null` reads as `null`), so a minimal API answers a JSON request body that holds one with 400.
- Minimal APIs bind no query value, route value or header to it: it has no conversion from `string`, no `TryParse` and no `BindAsync`. The constructor's parameter, `url`, matches no property, so `[AsParameters]` refuses the type as well, and a loader parameter of type `Href`, with or without `[AsParameters]`, stops the app at startup. Form binding builds one from a field named after the constructor's parameter (`next.url` for a property `Next`), checked for its shape only, so any `https:` URL fills it, and never from the field of the property's own name (`next`), which leaves an `init` property `null` and fails a positional record's post with 400. Keep `Href` out of `[FromForm]` inputs and take a `string`. A URL from the request, such as a `returnUrl`, stays a `string`: check it with `Page.IsLocalUrl` and redirect with `Page.LocalRedirect`.
- Two values are equal when their URLs are the same, character by character. `Value` and `ToString()` return the URL, and an `Href` converts to `string` wherever one is expected.

The name is in `Netjes`, which apps with implicit usings import everywhere: a file that also imports another namespace with a type named `Href` gets CS0104 for it. Qualify one of the two, or give one an alias (`using SiteHref = MyCms.Href;`).

## Metadata, sitemap and robots

### PageMetadata

```csharp
public sealed record PageMetadata
{
    public string? Title { get; init; }
    public string? Description { get; init; }
    public IReadOnlyList<string>? Keywords { get; init; }
    public PageMetadataRobots? Robots { get; init; }
    public PageMetadataAlternates? Alternates { get; init; }
    public PageMetadataOpenGraph? OpenGraph { get; init; }
    public PageMetadataTwitter? Twitter { get; init; }
    public string? ThemeColor { get; init; }
    public IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string>? Other { get; init; }
}

public sealed record PageMetadataRobots(bool Index = true, bool Follow = true);
public sealed record PageMetadataAlternates(string? Canonical = null, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string>? Languages = null);
public sealed record PageMetadataOpenGraph
{
    public string? Title { get; init; }
    public string? Description { get; init; }
    public string? Url { get; init; }
    public string? SiteName { get; init; }
    public string? Type { get; init; }
    public string? Locale { get; init; }
    public IReadOnlyList<PageMetadataImage>? Images { get; init; }
}
public sealed record PageMetadataImage(string Url, int? Width = null, int? Height = null, string? Alt = null);   // implicit conversion from string
public sealed record PageMetadataTwitter
{
    public string? Card { get; init; }   // summary, summary_large_image, app or player
    public string? Site { get; init; }
    public string? Creator { get; init; }
    public IReadOnlyList<PageMetadataImage>? Images { get; init; }   // a string converts to an image with only a URL
}
```

Head tags from C#, passed to `WithMetadata`. Properties left `null` leave the files' metadata as it is. `Other` adds `<meta name content>` tags, and `Alternates.Languages` adds a `<link rel="alternate" hreflang>` for each locale. A `PageMetadataImage` is written as `og:image` (or `twitter:image`) with its `Url`, followed by `og:image:width`, `og:image:height` and `og:image:alt` for an Open Graph image, or `twitter:image:alt` for a Twitter one, whichever are set. The Twitter tags that neither `Twitter` nor the files set fill in from Open Graph and the page's title and description once the two are merged, as in Next.js ([Open Graph and Twitter](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/metadata.md#open-graph-and-twitter)). The title, description and robots are also what the [client-rendered fallback](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/rendering-and-streaming.md#when-no-sidecar-is-ready) puts in its head.

### MapSitemap, MapRobotsTxt, ExcludeFromSitemap

```csharp
public static IEndpointConventionBuilder MapSitemap(this IEndpointRouteBuilder endpoints, Uri siteUrl, TimeSpan? cacheFor = null);
public static IEndpointConventionBuilder MapRobotsTxt(this IEndpointRouteBuilder endpoints, Uri siteUrl, IReadOnlyList<string>? disallow = null);
public static TBuilder ExcludeFromSitemap<TBuilder>(this TBuilder builder) where TBuilder : IEndpointConventionBuilder;
```

In the `Netjes` namespace (`SitemapEndpointRouteBuilderExtensions`), like Next.js's `app/sitemap.ts` and `app/robots.ts`.

- `MapSitemap` serves `/sitemap.xml`, for `GET` and `HEAD`: every page without route parameters, and dynamic pages through their `.StaticParams(...)`, as absolute URLs under `siteUrl` and the base path. Pages that require authorization (their own, or the fallback policy's unless they are `.AllowAnonymous()`) or call `.ExcludeFromSitemap()` are left out. The list of pages is built at most once per `cacheFor` (default an hour) and the response is sent with that `max-age`. Base paths are percent-encoded in the URLs. The XML is stored for the first eight base paths requested in each `cacheFor`; others, which a client can cause through `X-Forwarded-Prefix`, are built from the stored list on each request. Under a base path longer than 256 characters as the XML writes it (percent-encoded, with each `&` as `&amp;`), it answers 404 without building anything.
- `MapRobotsTxt` serves `/robots.txt`, for `GET` and `HEAD`: `User-agent: *`, a `Disallow` line for each path in `disallow` (or `Allow: /` without any), and a `Sitemap:` line with the sitemap's absolute URL, under `siteUrl` and the base path like `MapSitemap`'s.
- `netjes export` writes both files, since both carry `IncludeInExport`, unless the call is `.ExcludeFromExport()`. In the export, the sitemap lists the pages the export writes, in its order, without those marked `.ExcludeFromSitemap()`, so a page marked `.ExcludeFromExport()` is not listed. Both use the `siteUrl` passed in the Production environment, where the export runs, and the export logs a warning when it is a loopback address such as `http://localhost:5080` ([static export](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/static-export.md#sitemap-and-robotstxt)).

Both endpoints allow anonymous access, and answer a `HEAD` with the status and headers of a `GET`, without the body. Each answers one spelling of its path, as a page does: another case (`/Sitemap.xml`), or a trailing slash under `TrailingSlash.Never`, gets a 308 to `/sitemap.xml` or `/robots.txt`, as `RedirectLiteralCase` and `TrailingSlash` ask ([One URL per page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/routing.md#one-url-per-page)).

## Server actions

### MapAction

```csharp
public static RouteHandlerBuilder MapAction(this IEndpointRouteBuilder endpoints, string name, Delegate action)
```

A server action, the counterpart of a Next.js `'use server'` function: a `POST` endpoint at `/_netjes/actions/{name}`. `name` is letters, digits, `.`, `-` and `_` (`posts.create`); another character, or a name mapped twice, throws. The delegate binds like a minimal API handler (a JSON body, `[FromForm]` fields, services), and one minimal APIs cannot bind throws here, naming the action, as does a `[FromForm]` input with several public constructors or none, or an abstract or interface type, which form binding never builds. It returns a `ServerActionResult` or `ServerActionResult<T>`, which types the generated `serverActions` reference. Before the delegate runs, the DataAnnotations of its inputs, and then `IValidatableObject`, are checked, and failures come back as `ServerAction.Invalid` field errors, with or without `AddValidation()`; an attribute that cannot be read, on an input or on a derived type it lists with `[JsonDerivedType]`, throws here ([validation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/actions-and-forms.md#validation)). A `[FromForm]` input is never `null` unless the parameter is declared nullable: a post with none of its fields gets an empty input, checked like any other. Every call needs a valid antiforgery token and a same-origin request; `.DisableAntiforgery()` turns off the token check only. Request bodies are limited to `ActionBodySizeLimit` (1 MB) unless the action has its own limit ([body limits](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/actions-and-forms.md#body-limits)). Without JavaScript a form posts here too. An action that sets or deletes a cookie, such as signing in or out, makes the client router forget the pages it keeps for Back and Forward, in every tab of the app ([signing in and out](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/actions-and-forms.md#signing-in-and-out)).

### ServerAction

```csharp
public static class ServerAction
{
    public static ServerActionResult<TResult> Ok<TResult>(TResult result);
    public static ServerActionResult Ok();
    public static ServerActionResult Invalid(IDictionary<string, string[]> errors);
    public static ServerActionResult Invalid(string field, string message);
    public static ServerActionResult Forbidden();
    public static ServerActionResult NotFound();
    public static ServerActionResult Redirect(string location);
}
```

| Member | What it does |
|---|---|
| `Ok(result)` | Success; the client's call resolves to `{ ok: true, result }`. Typed by the result, for the generated reference. Without JavaScript the browser is redirected back to the form's page. |
| `Ok()` | Success with no result. |
| `Invalid(errors)`, `Invalid(field, message)` | Validation failed: 422 with the errors per field, field names written with the app's JSON naming policy. A call from the client resolves to `{ ok: false, errors }`, and `useAction`'s state also keeps what was typed; without JavaScript the form's page is rendered again with them. |
| `Forbidden()` | 403. A client call throws to the nearest error boundary; a post without JavaScript gets the error page. |
| `NotFound()` | 404, handled like `Forbidden()`. |
| `Redirect(location)` | Success; the client navigates to `location`. The same URL rules as `Page.Redirect`. |

### ServerActionResult and ServerActionResult&lt;TResult&gt;

```csharp
public sealed class ServerActionResult : IResult
{
    public ServerActionResult Revalidate(params string[] tags);
    public ServerActionResult RevalidatePath(params string[] paths);
    public ServerActionResult Refresh();
    public ServerActionResult Invalidate(params IReadOnlyList<object?>[] queryKeys);
    public ServerActionResult WithQuery(IReadOnlyList<object?> queryKey, object? data);
    public Task ExecuteAsync(HttpContext http);
}
```

`ServerActionResult<TResult>` has the same methods, returning `ServerActionResult<TResult>`, and converts from `ServerActionResult`, so one action can return `Ok(result)` or `Invalid(...)`.

| Method | What it does |
|---|---|
| `Revalidate(tags)` | Evicts every output-cache entry with these tags, then the client loads its page again: pages tagged with `CachePage`, and endpoints of the app tagged with `.CacheOutput(p => p.Tag(...))` ([endpoints that are not pages](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/caching.md#endpoints-that-are-not-pages)). |
| `RevalidatePath(paths)` | Evicts the output-cached pages at these paths (any query string, case and trailing slash aside), then the client loads its page again. It evicts pages only, never the entry of an endpoint that is not a page. |
| `Refresh()` | The client loads its current page again (every loader runs) once the action completes. |
| `Invalidate(queryKeys)` | Invalidates these TanStack Query keys, and those they prefix, on the client, so they are fetched again. |
| `WithQuery(queryKey, data)` | Sets a TanStack Query entry on the client, such as the updated record, without a fetch. Throws for an empty key. |

## Caching and drafts

### CachePage

```csharp
public static TBuilder CachePage<TBuilder>(this TBuilder builder, TimeSpan duration, params string[] tags)
    where TBuilder : IEndpointConventionBuilder
```

Output-caches the page for `duration`, tagged with `tags`, on ASP.NET Core output caching (`AddOutputCache()` and `UseOutputCache()`, after `UseNetjes()` and authentication), like incremental static regeneration. Entries are keyed by the page rules: the path and query as sent, document or payload, the layouts the client holds, the build. Pages under it never carry an antiforgery token. It also keys an endpoint that is no page but renders one (`Page.Render`). Each endpoint it is put on carries `duration` and `tags` as [`CachedPageMetadata`](#endpoint-metadata). It keeps its own copy of `tags`, so changing the array after the call changes neither the metadata nor the tags the entries get. In the Development environment nothing is stored: each request renders the page, which goes out `no-store, private` unless it sets its own `Cache-Control` ([caching](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/caching.md#in-the-development-environment)). See [caching](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/caching.md).

### IPageCache

```csharp
public interface IPageCache
{
    ValueTask RevalidateTagAsync(string tag, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
    ValueTask RevalidatePathAsync(string path, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
}
```

Evicts output-cache entries from anywhere (a webhook, a background job), like `revalidateTag` and `revalidatePath` outside actions. `RevalidateTagAsync` evicts every entry with the tag: pages tagged with `CachePage`, and endpoints of the app tagged with `.CacheOutput(p => p.Tag(...))`. `RevalidatePathAsync` evicts the document and the payloads of the page at the path, and never the entry of an endpoint that is not a page. Without output caching both do nothing. Inject it.

### IDraftMode

```csharp
public interface IDraftMode
{
    bool IsEnabled { get; }
    void Enable();
    void Disable();
}
```

Draft mode, like Next.js's `draftMode()`. Inject it into loaders to read `IsEnabled`, and call `Enable()` and `Disable()` from an endpoint you protect. `Enable()` sets a signed, `HttpOnly` cookie that lasts `DraftModeDuration`. While it is on, output caching is bypassed and nothing that answers the request is stored, and pages and the redirects loaders return go out `no-store, private`. See [caching](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/caching.md#draft-mode).

## Static export

```csharp
public static TBuilder StaticParams<TBuilder>(this TBuilder builder, Func<IServiceProvider, IEnumerable<object>> parameters)
    where TBuilder : IEndpointConventionBuilder;
public static RouteHandlerBuilder StaticParams<TService>(this RouteHandlerBuilder builder, Func<TService, IEnumerable<object>> parameters)
    where TService : notnull;
public static TBuilder ExcludeFromExport<TBuilder>(this TBuilder builder) where TBuilder : IEndpointConventionBuilder;
public static TBuilder IncludeInExport<TBuilder>(this TBuilder builder) where TBuilder : IEndpointConventionBuilder;
```

- `StaticParams` lists the route values a dynamic page is exported for, like `generateStaticParams`: one object per page (`new { slug = "hello" }`), with arrays for catch-all parameters. The second overload resolves `TService` for you. `MapSitemap` uses the same list.
- `ExcludeFromExport` leaves the page out of `netjes export`. On an endpoint marked `IncludeInExport`, such as `MapSitemap` or `MapRobotsTxt`, it leaves that endpoint's file out.
- `IncludeInExport` makes `netjes export` write an endpoint that is no page as a file at its URL: it requests it with a `GET` without a query string after the pages, and writes the body of its 200 byte for byte, without its headers, like a Next.js route handler with `dynamic = 'force-static'`. The endpoint must answer `GET`, have no route parameters, end in a file extension (`/llms.txt`, `/feeds/news.xml` under a route group) and allow anonymous requests, and no file of the client build may have its path; otherwise the export fails before it writes anything. The same goes for a path segment that cannot be a file name, a path another output file has or needs as a directory, and a Windows device name. Any status other than 200 fails the export, and an endpoint that reads the query string is warned about. `ExcludeFromExport` wins over it. `MapSitemap` and `MapRobotsTxt` carry it ([other endpoints as files](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/static-export.md#other-endpoints-as-files-includeinexport)).

See [static export](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/static-export.md).

## Localization

```csharp
public static IServiceCollection AddNetjesLocalization(this IServiceCollection services, Action<NetjesLocalizationOptions>? configure = null);
public static IApplicationBuilder UseNetjesLocalization(this IApplicationBuilder app);
public static IEndpointConventionBuilder MapLocaleRedirect(this IEndpointRouteBuilder endpoints);
```

- `AddNetjesLocalization` turns on locale routing: request localization driven only by the `[lang]` route value, with parent-culture fallback off. With it, the payload carries the locale, `<html lang>` follows it, and `useLocale()` returns it.
- `UseNetjesLocalization`, after `UseNetjes()`, sets the request culture from the route value. An unsupported locale gets the not-found page (in the default culture) on a page, and a bare 404 on any other endpoint with the parameter; a supported one in another case is replaced by its configured name.
- `MapLocaleRedirect` maps `/`, for `GET` and `HEAD`, to a redirect to the browser's best supported locale by `Accept-Language` (an `nl-BE` browser goes to `/nl`), else the default. Keep the pages under `app/[lang]/`: an `app/page.tsx` next to it ties with it for `/`, so ASP.NET Core answers 500 there, and Netjes reports it as a route warning ([An endpoint that ties with a page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/routing.md#an-endpoint-that-ties-with-a-page)).

`NetjesLocalizationOptions` has `SupportedCultures` (default `["en"]`, the first is the default) and `RouteParameter` (default `lang`). See [redirects, rewrites and headers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/redirects-rewrites-headers.md#internationalized-routing).

## Security

### GetCspNonce

```csharp
public static string GetCspNonce(this HttpContext http)
```

This request's Content-Security-Policy nonce, created on first use. Netjes puts it on every script and stylesheet it renders, and `useNonce()` returns it, so a policy you write yourself can allow exactly those. A document with a nonce is never stored in the output cache. With `NetjesOptions.ContentSecurityPolicy` containing `{nonce}`, Netjes calls it for you. See [security](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/security.md#content-security-policy).

### NetjesContentSecurityPolicy

```csharp
public static class NetjesContentSecurityPolicy
{
    public static string ScriptHashes { get; }
}
```

`ScriptHashes` holds the `script-src` sources that allow Netjes's fixed inline scripts by their hashes, for a policy without a nonce: one `'sha256-…'` per script, in its quotes and separated by spaces, as in `$"script-src 'self' {NetjesContentSecurityPolicy.ScriptHashes}; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'"`. A fixed script has the same text in every document. In this version there is one, the bootstrap that collects streamed `Page.Defer` values; a Netjes version that changes it or adds such a script changes the value. The scripts that deliver `Page.Defer` values, and React's scripts that reveal Suspense boundaries, differ from render to render, so no hash covers them. React's script for form actions that are functions is left out too, since its text follows the React version. It is a property, not a constant, because the compiler copies a constant's value into the assemblies that use it: an assembly compiled against one version of Netjes would keep that version's hashes when it runs with another. The npm package exports the same value as [`CSP_SCRIPT_HASHES`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/reference/react-api.md#csp_script_hashes). See [security](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/security.md#hash-based).

## Options

`NetjesOptions`, `NetjesMode` (`Development`, `Production`), `NetjesImageOptions`, `NetjesSecurityHeaderOptions`, `NetjesLocalizationOptions` and `SkiaImageOptions` are described in the [options reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/reference/options.md).

### TrailingSlash

```csharp
public enum TrailingSlash
{
    Ignore = 0,
    Never = 1,
}
```

`TrailingSlash` is the type of `NetjesOptions.TrailingSlash`, in the `Netjes` namespace: `Ignore` (0, the default) answers a page's URL with and without a trailing slash, and `Never` (1) answers one with a slash with a 308 to the URL without it. Next to it, `NetjesOptions.RedirectLiteralCase` (a `bool`, true by default) redirects another case of a page's literal segments to its file's spelling ([options](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/reference/options.md#routing), [One URL per page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/routing.md#one-url-per-page)).

Like `Href`, the name is in `Netjes`, which apps with implicit usings import everywhere: a file that also imports another namespace with a type named `TrailingSlash` gets CS0104 for it. Qualify one of the two, or give one an alias.

## Telemetry and headers

### NetjesTelemetry

```csharp
public static class NetjesTelemetry
{
    public const string Name = "Netjes";
}
```

The name of Netjes's `ActivitySource` and `Meter`: `.WithTracing(t => t.AddSource(NetjesTelemetry.Name))`, `.WithMetrics(m => m.AddMeter(NetjesTelemetry.Name))`. The spans and metrics are listed in [deployment](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/deployment.md#telemetry).

### NetjesHeaders

```csharp
public static class NetjesHeaders
{
    public const string Data = "X-Netjes-Data";
    public const string ServerTime = "X-Netjes-Now";
    public const string Segments = "X-Netjes-Segments";
    public const string Antiforgery = "X-Netjes-Antiforgery";
    public const string Cookies = "X-Netjes-Cookies";
}
```

The headers between the client router and the server, for tests and proxies.

| Constant | What it is |
|---|---|
| `Data` | Sent by the client router to get the page payload as JSON instead of a document. |
| `ServerTime` | On client payloads: the server's clock in Unix milliseconds, also on output-cached ones. |
| `Segments` | Sent by the client router with the keys of the layouts it holds. |
| `Antiforgery` | `invalid` on the 400 a client's action call gets when its antiforgery token was refused. |
| `Cookies` | `changed` on the response to a client's action call or form post that set or deleted a cookie other than the antiforgery cookie. |

## Images

### IImageProcessor and its types

```csharp
namespace Netjes.Images;

public interface IImageProcessor
{
    IReadOnlyList<string> OutputFormats { get; }
    ValueTask<ProcessedImage> ProcessAsync(ImageSource source, ImageTransform transform, CancellationToken cancellationToken);
}

public sealed record ImageSource(ReadOnlyMemory<byte> Content, string ContentType);
public sealed record ImageTransform(int Width, int Quality, string? Format);
public sealed record ProcessedImage(ReadOnlyMemory<byte> Content, string ContentType);
public sealed class ImageRejectedException(string message) : Exception(message);
public sealed class PassThroughImageProcessor : IImageProcessor;
```

The image endpoint hands each image to the registered `IImageProcessor` (a singleton). Register your own to resize and encode in another way.

- `OutputFormats`: the formats it can encode, preferred first (`image/webp`); the endpoint picks one the browser accepts.
- `ImageSource`: the original bytes, from `public/` or an allowed remote host, and the format they are (`image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif`, `image/webp` or `image/avif`), whatever the file's extension or the remote `Content-Type` said.
- `ImageTransform`: one of the configured widths (do not upscale past the source), the quality (1 to 100), and an output format from `OutputFormats`, or `null` to keep the source's.
- `ProcessedImage`: the bytes to send and their media type.
- `ImageRejectedException`: throw it to refuse an image (too many pixels, say); the endpoint answers with its message, 400 for a local image and 502 for a remote one.
- `PassThroughImageProcessor`: the default, which serves images unchanged (but cached).

### AddNetjesSkiaImages (Netjes.Images.SkiaSharp)

```csharp
public static IServiceCollection AddNetjesSkiaImages(this IServiceCollection services, Action<SkiaImageOptions>? configure = null)

namespace Netjes.Images.SkiaSharp;
public sealed class SkiaImageProcessor : IImageProcessor
{
    public SkiaImageProcessor(SkiaImageOptions options);
    public SkiaImageProcessor();
}
```

Replaces the image processor with `SkiaImageProcessor`, before or after `AddNetjes()`. It resizes to the requested width (never larger than the source), applies the EXIF orientation, decodes large JPEGs at a reduced size, and encodes WebP when the browser accepts it, else the source's format. It decodes PNG, JPEG and WebP only, and only bytes that start like the declared format; it refuses images whose header declares more than `MaxPixels` and images it cannot decode, and passes GIF (which may be animated) and AVIF through unchanged. See [images](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/images.md).

## Rendering seams

### ISsrRenderer

```csharp
namespace Netjes.Rendering;

public interface ISsrRenderer
{
    Task<string> RenderAsync(string payloadJson, CancellationToken cancellationToken);
    Task<Stream> RenderStreamAsync(string payloadJson, SsrStreamOptions options, CancellationToken cancellationToken); // default: buffers RenderAsync
    Task ResolveAsync(string renderId, string id, string? valueJson, string? error, CancellationToken cancellationToken); // default: does nothing
}

public sealed record SsrStreamOptions(bool WaitForAll, string? RenderId = null);
```

What renders a page payload (HTML-safe JSON) to an HTML document; by default the sidecar pool. Register your own to replace server rendering, as tests do to run the app without Node (see [testing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/testing.md#the-app-over-http)): the sidecar then does not start. `RenderStreamAsync` streams the shell first and each Suspense boundary as it resolves, and throws before it returns if the shell fails; `WaitForAll` asks for the complete document (crawlers, export), and `RenderId` is set when the payload has deferred values, which `ResolveAsync` delivers. An empty `error` in `ResolveAsync` is a failure whose message is withheld: pass it on as it is, so that the browser rejects the value with its own stand-in, marked `withheld`.

### SsrRenderException

```csharp
public sealed class SsrRenderException(string message, string? jsStack, Exception? inner = null) : Exception
{
    public string? JsStack { get; }
}
```

Server rendering failed in the Node sidecar, or the sidecar could not be reached or took too long. `JsStack` holds the JavaScript stack when there is one; error pages show it in development.

## Endpoint metadata

```csharp
namespace Netjes.Routing;

public sealed class PageRouteMetadata
{
    public string Pattern { get; }
    public bool IsLoader { get; }
}

public sealed class CachedPageMetadata
{
    public TimeSpan Duration { get; }
    public IReadOnlyList<string> Tags { get; }
}
```

What app code and tests read from the endpoints to find the app's pages and their loaders, as `netjes routes` does, and the settings `CachePage` was given. The report's output caching (`cached` in `--json`) does not come from `CachedPageMetadata`: it is true under any output-cache policy on the endpoint, while `CachedPageMetadata` is there only under `CachePage` ([the route table](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/routing.md#the-route-table)). Netjes puts both on the endpoints, and their constructors are internal.

- `PageRouteMetadata` is on every endpoint that serves a page: the `GET` and `HEAD` endpoint of a page file or of `MapPageLoader`, and the `POST` endpoint of `MapPageAction`. `Pattern` is the page's URL as its file names it (`/blog/[slug]`), without the prefix of a route group the endpoint is mapped in, which the endpoint's own route pattern includes. `IsLoader` is true on the endpoint `MapPageLoader` maps, and false on a page file's own endpoint (a page without a loader) and on a page action's. No other endpoint carries it: not the not-found fallback, a server action, a minimal API that returns `Page.Render`, or the endpoints Netjes maps, such as `/_netjes/image`, and `/sitemap.xml` from `MapSitemap`.
- `CachedPageMetadata` is on every endpoint `CachePage` is put on (a page loader, each file page under `MapPages().CachePage(...)`, a minimal API that returns `Page.Render`, the endpoints of a route group), with the `duration` and the `tags` it was given, in the order given. An endpoint output-cached without `CachePage` (`CacheOutput`, `[OutputCache]`, a base policy) carries none. A `CacheOutput(...)` after `CachePage` on the same endpoint replaces the policy `CachePage` set, and the metadata still holds what `CachePage` was given ([caching](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/caching.md#under-any-output-caching)).

Read them from `Endpoint.Metadata` once the app has started, in a test through the [factory](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/testing.md#the-app-over-http) and in the app through an injected `EndpointDataSource`:

```csharp
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Routing;
using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;
using Netjes.Routing;

public sealed class CachedPageTests(AppFactory app) : IClassFixture<AppFactory>
{
    [Fact]
    public void EveryCachedPage_HasATagToRevalidateItBy()
    {
        foreach (var endpoint in app.Services.GetRequiredService<EndpointDataSource>().Endpoints)
        {
            if (endpoint.Metadata.GetMetadata<PageRouteMetadata>() is { } page
                && endpoint.Metadata.GetMetadata<CachedPageMetadata>() is { } cached)
            {
                Assert.True(cached.Tags.Count > 0, $"{page.Pattern} is cached for {cached.Duration} without a tag.");
            }
        }
    }
}
```

A page with a page action has two endpoints with the same `Pattern`, its `GET` one and the action's `POST` one, so a walk that counts pages takes the endpoints whose `IHttpMethodMetadata` lists `GET`. The endpoints' display names, such as `Page /blog/[slug]`, are not part of the API.

## Route errors

```csharp
namespace Netjes.Routing;

public sealed class RouteConflictException(string message) : Exception;
public sealed class InvalidPageFileException(string message) : Exception;
```

Netjes throws these when the files in `app/` break the file conventions. The message names the files and what to change.

- `RouteConflictException`: two pages of one shape, such as `app/[lang]/about/page.tsx` and `app/[slug]/about/page.tsx`, or two files for one convention in one folder, such as `page.tsx` and `page.jsx`. Pages that only overlap, such as `[id]` next to `[...rest]`, get a [route warning](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/routing.md#two-pages-that-match-the-same-urls) instead.
- `InvalidPageFileException`: a file name the conventions do not allow, such as a catch-all that is not the last segment, a `global-error` file below the app root, or a `route.ts` file. `UseNetjes` also throws it for page files in a `pages/` folder, which Netjes does not route ([Routing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/routing.md#what-is-not-there)).

`MapPages` reads the routes as the app starts, from `app/` in development and from the client build's manifest in production, so either exception stops the app there, and a test that starts the app can catch it by type. When a file changes while the development server runs, Netjes logs the error instead and keeps the previous routes.

The route table that Netjes builds from `app/` is not part of the API. A tool that needs the routes runs `netjes routes --json` ([the netjes command](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/reference/cli.md#netjes-routes)); app code and tests read the pages from their endpoints ([endpoint metadata](#endpoint-metadata)).

<!-- Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/reference/options.md -->

# Options

This page lists every setting of the Netjes NuGet packages: each `NetjesOptions` property with its configuration key, type, default and effect, the nested image and security-header options, the options that are set in code only, the `Netjes:PublicConfig` section, the environment variables Netjes reads, and the MSBuild properties of `build/Netjes.targets`. It is a reference for app developers; the guides explain when to use each. The Vite plugin's options are in the [Vite plugin reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/reference/vite-plugin.md), the CLI's in the [CLI reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/reference/cli.md).

## Where options come from

`AddNetjes()` binds `NetjesOptions` from the `Netjes` configuration section, so every ASP.NET Core configuration source can set them, and then runs the delegate you pass, which wins:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddNetjes(options =>
{
    options.SidecarProcesses = 4;
    options.ContentSecurityPolicy = "script-src 'nonce-{nonce}' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'";
});
```

```json
{
  "Netjes": {
    "SidecarProcesses": 4,
    "RenderTimeout": "00:00:20",
    "Images": { "RemoteHosts": ["images.example.com"] },
    "SecurityHeaders": { "DraftFrameAncestors": ["https://cms.example"] }
  }
}
```

The key of a property is `Netjes:<Name>`, and of a nested one `Netjes:Images:<Name>` or `Netjes:SecurityHeaders:<Name>`. In environment variables the separator is a double underscore (`Netjes__SidecarProcesses=4`, `Netjes__Images__RemoteHosts__0=images.example.com`). Durations are written `hh:mm:ss`.

Configuration adds list items to what a list holds already, while the delegate replaces the list. So configured `PrivateFormFields` are added to the default words. `Images:Widths` and `Images:Qualities` get their defaults only when nothing set them, so configured values replace those.

## NetjesOptions

### Files and mode

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Root` | `string?` | the content root | The folder that holds `package.json`, `vite.config.ts` and `app/`. Relative to the content root. |
| `AppDirectory` | `string` | `app` | The folder of page files, relative to `Root`. Must match the Vite plugin's `appDir`. |
| `DistDirectory` | `string` | `dist` | Where the build is, relative to `Root`: `client/` (with Vite's manifest in `client/.vite/`) and `server/`. |
| `PublicDirectory` | `string` | `public` | Static files served as they are in development, relative to `Root`. In production Vite has copied them into the client build. |
| `Mode` | `NetjesMode?` | `Development` in the Development environment, else `Production` | `Development` compiles pages on demand with the Vite dev server and reads the routes from the files in `app/`; `Production` serves the build in `dist/` and reads the routes from its manifest. |
| `TypesFile` | `string?` | `generated/netjes.ts` | The generated TypeScript, relative to `Root`. Written at startup in development when it changed, and by `netjes generate`. `null` (in code) turns generation off. |

### Routing

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `RedirectLiteralCase` | `bool` | `true` | A `GET` or `HEAD` for a page in another case of the literal segments its file names (`/About` for `app/about/page.tsx`) answers 308 with the file's spelling (`/about`); a client navigation gets a redirect payload. So do the `/robots.txt` and `/sitemap.xml` that `MapRobotsTxt` and `MapSitemap` serve, in another case of their literal segments. Route values, the query string, the base path and, under `TrailingSlash.Ignore`, a trailing slash stay as they were sent. Only the URL the client sent is redirected: not a rewritten or re-executed request, nor any on TestServer. `false` answers every case, as ASP.NET Core routing does. See [One URL per page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/routing.md#one-url-per-page). |
| `TrailingSlash` | `TrailingSlash` | `Ignore` | `Ignore` answers `/about` and `/about/` alike. `Never` answers a `GET` or `HEAD` for `/about/` with a 308 to `/about`, for the same kinds of requests as `RedirectLiteralCase` (the URL the client sent, for a page or for the `/robots.txt` and `/sitemap.xml` that `MapRobotsTxt` and `MapSitemap` serve), whether `RedirectLiteralCase` is on or off; a catch-all's value loses its last slash, and `/` stays. Set it in configuration as `Netjes:TrailingSlash=Never`. |

### Rendering and the sidecar

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NodeExecutable` | `string` | `node` | The Node.js executable that runs the sidecar processes. When it cannot be started, the app logs that in one line, naming this setting, and stops with exit code 1. |
| `SidecarScript` | `string?` | the `netjes` package's `sidecar/server.mjs` in development (found in `node_modules` here or above), `dist/server/netjes-sidecar.mjs` in production | The sidecar script. Relative to `Root`. When it is not there, the app says to run `npm install` (development) or `npm run build` (production), in one line, and stops with exit code 1. A script of your own must answer `GET /health`, with any status and without reading a request body: in production Netjes sends it to a process that has answered no render for 5 seconds, and restarts one that gives no answer (see `RenderTimeout`). The default script answers it. |
| `SidecarProcesses` | `int` | `1` | How many Node processes render pages in production. Development always runs one. Less than 1 stops the app at startup. See [rendering](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/rendering-and-streaming.md#the-sidecar-pool). |
| `ViteDevPort` | `int` | `5173` | The Vite dev server's port in development. When something else has it, such as another app's Vite dev server, the app logs that in one line, naming the port and this setting, and stops with exit code 1. |
| `StartupTimeout` | `TimeSpan` | 60 s | How long the sidecar processes may take to report ready at startup; past it the app does not start. |
| `RenderTimeout` | `TimeSpan` | 15 s | How long a render may take to produce the shell of a streamed document (everything outside Suspense boundaries that are still waiting). Also how long a render waits for a restarting process; a complete document waits up to `StreamTimeout`. In production also how long a health ping waits for an answer, and never less than 5 seconds: a process that answers nothing in that time is killed and restarted. See [rendering](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/rendering-and-streaming.md#restarts). |
| `StreamTimeout` | `TimeSpan` | 60 s | How long a whole document may take, Suspense boundaries and `Page.Defer` values included; a deferred value not there by then fails. Complete documents (crawlers, `StreamDocuments = false`, export) wait up to this long. |
| `StreamDocuments` | `bool` | `true` | Stream documents: the shell first, with fallbacks for what is still waiting, the rest as it is ready. `false` sends every document complete. |
| `CrawlerUserAgents` | `string` | a regular expression matching search engine bots, social previews, validators and Lighthouse | A regular expression, matched without regard to case against the `User-Agent`; matching requests get complete documents. |
| `ClientRenderFallback` | `bool` | `true` | In production, a document request that finds no sidecar process ready is answered with a shell .NET writes, and the browser renders the page. `false` waits for a restart and shows the error page if none comes in time. See [rendering](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/rendering-and-streaming.md#when-no-sidecar-is-ready). |
| `Lang` | `string` | `en` | The `lang` attribute of `<html>`. With `AddNetjesLocalization` the request's locale is used instead. |
| `IncludeErrorDetails` | `bool?` | `true` in the Development environment, else `false` | Show exception messages and stacks in error pages and in failed actions' and deferred values' messages. Without them, an exception's message stays on the server: an error page gets the status's reason phrase, a failed deferred value `Something went wrong` and a server action call Netjes's own message, each with `withheld` true ([`ErrorPageProps`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/reference/react-api.md#errorpageprops)). The one case that differs is a 4xx from a server action call made by the client, such as a `BadHttpRequestException`, whose message is always sent. |

### Actions and forms

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AllowedActionOrigins` | `IReadOnlyList<string>` | none | Origins besides the request's own host that may call server actions and post to page actions, such as `https://shop.example`. A request the browser marks `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` is refused whatever its origin. Prefer forwarded headers, so the app sees its public host. |
| `ActionBodySizeLimit` | `long?` | `1048576` (1 MB) | The largest request body a server action (`MapAction`) accepts, in bytes; larger ones get 413. It only lowers the server's own limit, never raises it. `null` (or an empty value in configuration) leaves the server's limit. Page actions keep the server's limit. An action with its own `[RequestSizeLimit]` or `[DisableRequestSizeLimit]` uses that. |
| `PrivateFormFields` | `IReadOnlyList<string>` | `password`, `passwd`, `pwd`, `pass`, `pw`, `passcode`, `passphrase`, `secret`, `token`, `apikey`, `privatekey`, `credential`, `pin`, `otp`, `totp`, `mfa`, `recovery`, `cvc`, `cvv`, `csc`, `cc`, `card`, `iban`, `ssn`, `bsn` | Words that mark a form field as private: a failed action never hands its value back. Compared without regard to case; words of five letters or more match anywhere in a name, shorter ones as a word of it or at a word's start or end. Configuration adds words to this list; the delegate replaces it. See [what a failed post hands back](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/actions-and-forms.md#what-a-failed-post-hands-back). |

### Security

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ContentSecurityPolicy` | `string?` | `null`: no policy | A Content-Security-Policy for documents. With `{nonce}`, each document gets a nonce in its place and on everything Netjes renders, and is never output-cached. Without it (hash-based), no nonce is made and pages can be cached, but must not stream, and the policy's `script-src` must list the hashes of Netjes's inline scripts: `$"script-src 'self' {NetjesContentSecurityPolicy.ScriptHashes}"`. When the policy has no `frame-ancestors`, Netjes adds `frame-ancestors 'self'`, with the `SecurityHeaders.DraftFrameAncestors` sites in draft mode, unless the app sent `X-Frame-Options` or `SecurityHeaders.Enabled` is false. Not sent when the app set the header itself. It goes out as written in every environment, so in Development it also has to allow the Vite dev server's scripts, its socket, the styles inlined there, and the images and fonts it serves ([in development](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/security.md#in-development)). When the policy on a document, this one or the app's own, refuses what the document needs, Netjes logs a warning once per policy ([what Netjes checks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/security.md#what-netjes-checks)). See [security](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/security.md#content-security-policy). |
| `SecurityHeaders` | `NetjesSecurityHeaderOptions` | below | The headers Netjes adds: `nosniff` to every response through `UseNetjes()`, the rest to documents. |
| `SegmentKeySecret` | `string?` | random per process | The secret that signs layout keys, at least 32 bytes of UTF-8 (shorter stops the app at startup). Set the same value on every instance so they accept each other's keys and share cached payloads that reuse layouts. See [deployment](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/deployment.md#the-segment-key-secret). |

### Caching, drafts and telemetry

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DraftModeDuration` | `TimeSpan` | 1 hour | How long `IDraftMode.Enable()` keeps draft mode on. |
| `CollectWebVitals` | `bool` | `false` | Accept Core Web Vitals from `<WebVitals />` at `/_netjes/vitals` (mapped by `MapPages()`) and record them as `netjes.web_vitals.*` histograms. |

### Images

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Images` | `NetjesImageOptions` | below | The `<Image>` endpoint. |

### Shared props (code only)

| Member | Type | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `UseSharedProps<T>(Func<HttpContext, ValueTask<T>> factory)` | method, returns the options | Props for every page and layout, read with `useSharedProps(sharedProps)`, and typed as `sharedProps` in the generated file. |
| `SharedProps` | `Func<HttpContext, ValueTask<object?>>?` | The same, untyped: the generated file does not know their shape. Setting it clears `SharedPropsType`. |
| `SharedPropsType` | `Type?` (read-only) | The type `UseSharedProps<T>` was called with; `null` when untyped. |

Output-cached pages store the shared props with the page, so they must not depend on cookies or other per-visitor state; see [caching](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/caching.md#shared-props-and-cookies).

## NetjesImageOptions (`Netjes:Images`)

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Widths` | `int[]` | Next.js's device and image sizes: 16, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 256, 384, 640, 750, 828, 1080, 1200, 1920, 2048, 3840 | The only widths the endpoint produces; `<Image>` builds its `srcset` from them. Configured widths replace the defaults. |
| `Qualities` | `int[]` | `[75]` | The qualities the endpoint accepts besides `DefaultQuality`; `<Image quality>` rounds to the nearest. Configured ones replace the default. |
| `DefaultQuality` | `int` | `75` | The quality when a request names none. |
| `RemoteHosts` | `string[]` | none | Hosts remote images may come from: `images.example.com`, or `*.example.com` for its subdomains. Nothing else is fetched. |
| `RemoteRequireHttps` | `bool` | `true` | Fetch remote images over https only. |
| `RemotePorts` | `int[]` | none | Ports remote images may come from besides the scheme's default. |
| `RemoteTimeout` | `TimeSpan` | 10 s | How long fetching a remote image may take, headers and body together; past it, 504. |
| `MaxSourceBytes` | `long` | `20971520` (20 MB) | The largest source image read, local or remote. |
| `MaxConcurrency` | `int` | one per CPU | How many images are read and processed at once. |
| `MaxRemoteFetches` | `int` | `16` | How many remote images are fetched at once, in slots of their own, kept until the image is processed. |
| `MaxQueue` | `int` | `1000` | How many requests may wait for a slot, in each of the two pools; past it, 503 with `Retry-After`. |
| `CacheDuration` | `TimeSpan` | 7 days | How long browsers and the output cache keep an optimised image. |
| `AllowSvg` | `bool` | `false` | Serve SVG files, unprocessed and sandboxed. Off because SVG can carry script. |
| `Path` | `string` | `/_netjes/image` | The endpoint's path, used with one leading slash and none trailing. Other spellings of it are refused. |

The [images guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/images.md) explains the limits and what they cost in memory.

## NetjesSecurityHeaderOptions (`Netjes:SecurityHeaders`)

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Enabled` | `bool` | `true` | Add `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` to every response that passes through `UseNetjes()`, and `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin` and framing headers to documents, each unless the app set it. Framing is same-origin (`X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN`, `frame-ancestors 'self'` in Netjes's policy); with `frame-ancestors` in a policy that goes out, documents get the `X-Frame-Options` it implies instead, `DENY` or `SAMEORIGIN`, and an app that sends `X-Frame-Options` keeps its own ([security](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/security.md#security-headers)). `false` adds none; the image endpoint keeps its own `nosniff` and sandboxing policy. |
| `DraftFrameAncestors` | `string[]` | none | Sites that may frame pages in draft mode, such as a CMS's preview: each one CSP source (`https://cms.example`, `https://*.cms.example`); anything else stops the app at startup. Ignored when the app sends its own `X-Frame-Options` or `Content-Security-Policy`, or has `frame-ancestors` in `ContentSecurityPolicy`. |

See [security](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/security.md#security-headers).

## Options set in code only

These are not bound from configuration.

### NetjesLocalizationOptions

`services.AddNetjesLocalization(options => ...)`:

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SupportedCultures` | `string[]` | `["en"]` | The locales, by culture name. The first is the default. A name matches only that culture exactly. |
| `RouteParameter` | `string` | `lang` | The route parameter that holds the locale: `app/[lang]/...`. |

### SkiaImageOptions

`services.AddNetjesSkiaImages(options => ...)`, from `Netjes.Images.SkiaSharp`:

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MaxPixels` | `long` | `40000000` | Images whose header declares more pixels are refused before decoding (about 160 MB decoded at the default). |
| `MaxConcurrency` | `int` | one per CPU | How many images are decoded and encoded at once; the rest wait. `Netjes:Images:MaxConcurrency` limits the whole endpoint, reading included. |

## Netjes:PublicConfig

A configuration section sent to the browser with the first document and read with `usePublicConfig(schema)`, like Next.js's `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variables but at runtime, so one build runs in every environment. Keys follow the app's JSON naming policy (camelCase by default), values are strings (configuration has no other type; use coercing schemas), and numbered keys become arrays. Everything in it is public. See [data loading](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/data-loading.md).

```json
{ "Netjes": { "PublicConfig": { "ApiBase": "https://api.example.com", "Features": { "Search": "true" } } } }
```

## Environment variables

| Variable | Read by | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `NETJES_COMMAND`, `NETJES_OUTPUT`, `NETJES_CHECK` | the app | Set by the `netjes` CLI to run the app once for `generate`, `routes` or `export`. Read only from the process environment, never from other configuration. |
| `NETJES_VITE_HOST` | the sidecar, in development | The Vite dev server's host. Unset, it listens on `localhost`; `0.0.0.0` exposes it to the network (see [security](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/security.md#the-development-server)). |
| `NETJES_VITE_ORIGIN` | the sidecar, in development | The origin browsers load modules from, when it is not `http://localhost:<ViteDevPort>` (a container, a remote machine). |
| `NETJES_TOKEN` | the sidecar | The token every request to it must carry. Netjes sets it; set it yourself only to run `sidecar/server.mjs` by hand. |
| `DOTNET_USE_POLLING_FILE_WATCHER` | ASP.NET Core | In development, polls `app/` for changes (every four seconds) instead of using file system events; the template's development image sets it. |

Netjes passes the sidecar its other settings (mode, root, ports, timeouts) itself.

## MSBuild properties

Set in the app's project file, read by `build/Netjes.targets`, which the Netjes package imports into the project:

| Property | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `NetjesRoot` | the project's folder | Where `package.json` and `dist/` are. |
| `NetjesBuildCommand` | `npm run build` | The client build that `dotnet publish` runs. |
| `NetjesSkipClientBuild` | unset | `true` publishes the `dist/` that is already there instead of building it. |

The targets also keep `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `test-results/`, `playwright-report/` and `publish/` out of the project's items, keep `package.json`, `package-lock.json` and `tsconfig.json` out of the output, and add `using Netjes;` when implicit usings are on. See [deployment](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/deployment.md#build-and-publish).

<!-- Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/reference/cli.md -->

# The netjes command

`netjes` comes with the `netjes` npm package. It creates apps, runs them in development and production, builds them, and asks the app itself for its generated types and its route table ([ADR 0007](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0007-a-node-cli-that-asks-the-app.md)).

In an app, run it with `npx netjes <command>` or through the npm scripts the template sets up (`npm run dev`, `npm run generate`, `npm run routes`). It needs Node.js `^22.22.2 || ^24.15.0 || >=26.0.0` (the range the `netjes` package and the app template declare as `engines`) and the .NET 10 SDK or newer; `netjes info` checks both.

```text
netjes <command> [arguments] [options]
netjes help [<command>]
netjes --version
```

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`new <dir>`](#netjes-new) | Create an app: ASP.NET Core with React pages, Tailwind CSS, TanStack Query, zod and Vitest |
| [`dev`](#netjes-dev) | Run the app in Development: `dotnet watch` with C# hot reload, Vite HMR for pages |
| [`build`](#netjes-build) | Generate the types, then build the client and server bundles into `dist/` |
| [`start`](#netjes-start) | Run the app in Production, from a build or a published app |
| [`generate`](#netjes-generate) | Write `generated/netjes.ts` from the C# types |
| [`routes`](#netjes-routes) | Print the route table and its warnings, as the app sees them |
| [`export [dir]`](#netjes-export) | Build, then write every page as static HTML into a folder |
| [`info`](#netjes-info) | Check the tools and the project setup |
| [`agents [dir]`](#netjes-agents) | Add `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and the Netjes skill for coding agents to an existing app |

`netjes`, `netjes help` and `netjes --help` list the commands and the options every command takes, and end with a link to this page at the release tag of the installed version (`https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/v<version>/docs/reference/cli.md`), which describes that version's commands and options. `netjes help <command>`, `netjes <command> --help` and `netjes <command> -h` print a command's usage, its options with their defaults, and examples.

## Options and arguments

Every command takes these:

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--cwd <dir>` | Run in another directory, usually the app's folder. It must exist. | the current directory |
| `-h`, `--help` | Show help, for the command when one is given. | |
| `-v`, `--version` | Print the version of netjes and exit. | |

Options can come before or after the command and its arguments. `--name Shop` and `--name=Shop` are the same; a value that starts with `-` needs the `=` form (`--cwd=-site`). `--` ends the options: what follows is an argument even if it starts with `-`.

Each command accepts only its own options and the ones above. An unknown command or option, an option without its value, a value for a flag, or one argument too many is a usage error: netjes prints one line on stderr, with a suggestion when one is close, starts nothing, and exits 1.

```console
$ netjes nwe my-shop
netjes: unknown command 'nwe'; did you mean `netjes new`?
$ netjes generate --chek
netjes generate: unknown option '--chek'; did you mean '--check'?
```

## netjes new

```text
netjes new <dir> [--name <Name>] [--packages] [--skip-install]
```

Creates an app in `<dir>`, runs `npm install` in it, and prints where things are and what to run next.

| Argument or option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `<dir>` | The folder to create the app in. It must not exist yet, or be empty. | asked for in a terminal; required otherwise |
| `--name <Name>` | The .NET project name and root namespace. | the folder name in PascalCase: `my-shop` gives `MyShop` |
| `--packages` | Use the Netjes NuGet and npm packages even when netjes runs from a Netjes checkout. | off; outside a checkout the packages are used anyway |
| `--skip-install` | Do not run `npm install` in the new app. | off |

```bash
npx netjes new my-shop
npx netjes new my-shop --name Shop --skip-install
```

Names. The project gets three names: a .NET name (the `.csproj`, the root namespace and the assembly), an npm package name and a title. From the folder name `my-shop` they are `MyShop`, `my-shop` and `My Shop`; a name that starts with a digit gets `App` in front (`1shop` gives `App1shop`), and accents are dropped (`Mijn Café` gives `MijnCafe`, `mijn-cafe` and `Mijn Cafe`). `--name` is used as given for the .NET name, and must be letters and digits starting with a letter; the npm name and the title are made from it (`--name MyShop` gives `my-shop` and `My Shop`). netjes refuses, before it writes anything:

- `--name` with anything other than letters and digits, or starting with a digit (`--name my-shop`; it suggests `--name MyShop`);
- a folder name with no ASCII letters or digits, unless `--name` is given;
- a C# keyword as `--name`, such as `class` or `event` (a keyword cannot name a namespace);
- the name of a type the app's code uses by its simple name: `Program`, `SiteProps`, `Page`, `ServerAction`, `WebApplication`, `ValueTask`, `DateTimeOffset`, `TimeProvider`, `IEndpointRouteBuilder` and `FromFormAttribute`. A root namespace of that name hides the type, and the build fails (CS0101, CS0118 or CS0234). A folder named `page` is refused for the same reason, as it gives `Page`;
- an npm name that is one of the app's own dependencies, such as `react`, `vite` or `netjes` (npm refuses to install a package into one of the same name).

How the app references Netjes. From the published package, the `.csproj` gets `<PackageReference Include="Netjes" Version="[x.y.z]" />` and `package.json` gets `"netjes": "x.y.z"`, both the exact version of the netjes that ran `new`: the C# and npm halves speak one protocol. Run from a Netjes checkout (contributors), it references that checkout instead (a `ProjectReference` and a `file:` dependency), unless `--packages` is given. Such an app imports the package's compiled modules from the checkout's `packages/netjes/dist/`, so build them first, with `npm ci && npm run build` at the checkout's root, and again after changing `packages/netjes`.

Without `<dir>`, netjes asks for the folder when stdin and stdout are a terminal, and fails as a usage error otherwise, so scripts and CI never hang on a prompt. An empty answer or Ctrl+D at the prompt is a usage error too; Ctrl+C stops netjes with exit code 130, before it writes anything.

When `npm install` fails, the app stays where it is: netjes says so on stderr and exits with npm's exit code. Fix what npm reported, then run `npm install` in the app.

## netjes dev

```text
netjes dev [--no-watch]
```

Runs `dotnet watch run` in Development. The app starts its Node sidecar, which runs the Vite dev server, so C# changes hot reload and pages update through Vite HMR. The app listens on `http://localhost:5080` unless `ASPNETCORE_URLS` is set; the Vite dev server uses port 5173 (`Netjes:ViteDevPort`).

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--no-watch` | Run once with `dotnet run` instead of `dotnet watch`. | off |

```bash
netjes dev
ASPNETCORE_URLS=http://localhost:3000 netjes dev
```

There is no `--port` option (nor `-p`): the app's URL sets the port, so `netjes dev --port 3000` fails and says to set `ASPNETCORE_URLS=http://localhost:3000` when you run `netjes dev`. `netjes start` answers the same way. netjes runs the app without its launch profiles, so a profile's `applicationUrl` does not apply either.

Before it starts anything, netjes checks that the folder has a `.csproj`, that `netjes` and `vite` are installed (`npm install`), that the app's port is free when the app gets one localhost URL, and that the Vite dev server's port is free. It reads Vite's port from the same settings as the app: `Netjes__ViteDevPort` from the environment, else `Netjes:ViteDevPort` from `appsettings.Development.json` (or the file of the environment `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT` names) or `appsettings.json`, else 5173. A port the app sets in code is not seen: netjes checks the one it read instead, and the app itself reports when the port it set is taken. Setting `Netjes__ViteDevPort` to the same port makes netjes check that one. Each of the checks fails with one line saying what to do, and exit code 1:

```text
netjes dev: port 5173 is in use, and the Vite dev server needs it; stop what is using it, or move Vite to another port: Netjes__ViteDevPort=5174 netjes dev
```
