Both files use the `siteUrl` of the Production environment, so set the static host's URL for the export (`SiteUrl=https://www.example.com npx netjes export` when the app reads `app.Configuration["SiteUrl"]`); a loopback one, such as a `http://localhost:5080` fallback, is written and warned about.

The export requests every URL without a query string, and a static host serves each file for every query string. A page whose loader, or a layout loader above it, reads the query string is still exported, as the page without one, and the export logs a warning in `Netjes.Export.QueryString`. To export a page for each value, make it a route parameter with `.StaticParams(...)` (`/blog/tags/[tag]`, not `/blog?tag=`); to keep the page on a server, exclude it. A loader parameter with no default value and a type that is not nullable (`int page`, `string q`) requires the value: without one the page answers 400 and the export fails, so give it a default value or a nullable type (`int page = 1`, `string? q`) to export the page without one. On an exported page `useSearchParams()` sees no query string either, whatever the address bar shows: read `window.location.search` in an effect there, and parse it with the same schema.

## Sitemap and robots

`app.MapSitemap(siteUrl)` serves `/sitemap.xml` from the route table (dynamic pages through `.StaticParams`, pages that need authorization or call `.ExcludeFromSitemap()` left out) and `app.MapRobotsTxt(siteUrl, disallow)` serves `/robots.txt`. `netjes export` writes both ([Static export](#static-export)).

Leave `/_netjes/` out of `disallow`: `<Image>` serves every image through `/_netjes/image`, so a crawler that may not fetch it cannot index your images. The other endpoints there take posts or hand out an antiforgery token, which a crawler has no use for. Under a base path, `disallow` paths are written as given, so include the base path in them. See [Metadata](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/guides/metadata.md).

## More

[Caching](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/guides/caching.md), [Rendering and streaming](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/guides/rendering-and-streaming.md) and [Static export](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/guides/static-export.md) in the guides.

<!-- Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/packages/netjes/skills/netjes/references/testing.md -->

# Testing

Test first: write the test, watch it fail for the reason you expect, then change the code. Assert what a user or a browser can observe (rendered text, roles, URLs, status codes, the props a page receives), not internals.

## Components and pages: Vitest

`netjes()` in `vite.config.ts` sets up Vitest: jsdom, Testing Library cleanup (a config with `setupFiles` of its own lists `netjes/testing/setup` in them), `e2e/`, `dist/`, `bin/` and `obj/` excluded, and in every app a setup file of Netjes's own, which lets Testing Library work with fake timers and hands `createTestApp` the app's query defaults. Inline `test.projects` that share the root's Vite server, Vitest 5's default, get none of this: set `sharedViteServer: false` in the root's `test` options. Tests sit next to the code as `*.test.tsx` and run with `npm test`.

```tsx
import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';
import { createTestApp } from 'netjes/testing';
import { expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { HelloForm } from './HelloForm.tsx';

it('shows the validation error from C# next to the field', async () => {
  const app = createTestApp({
    actions: { 'home.greet': () => ({ ok: false, status: 422, errors: { name: ['Tell us your name.'] } }) },
  });
  render(<HelloForm />, { wrapper: app.Wrapper });

  await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Say hello' }));

  expect(await screen.findByText('Tell us your name.')).toBeDefined();
});
```

`createTestApp({ url, params, shared, queries, defaultOptions, navigation, antiforgery, actions })` returns `{ Wrapper, navigations, queryClient }`:

- `url` and `params` set what `usePathname`, `useSearchParams` and `useParams` see; `shared` is what `useSharedProps` returns; `queries: [{ key, data }]` seeds TanStack Query as a loader's `.WithQuery` would.
- The `QueryClient` starts from the app's `netjes({ query: { defaultOptions } })`: a failed query or mutation is tried as often as in the app, with no wait between the tries, so the test sees the error the app shows after its last try. `defaultOptions` goes over them: `{ queries: { retry: false } }` shows the error after the first request. Seeded data is fresh for the app's `staleTime` from when `createTestApp()` is called: with a `staleTime` of 0, or in a component rendered after a fake clock moved past it, a seeded query is fetched again as it mounts; answer that request (MSW) or pass `{ queries: { staleTime: 60_000 } }`.
- `actions` answers server action calls by name: `{ ok: true, result }` or `{ ok: false, status: 422, errors }` (add `fields: ['email']` to name the fields a failed state's `values` keep, as the server does). A failure other than a 422 throws a `ServerActionError`, withheld unless the answer has the `message` the server would send: `{ ok: false, status: 403, errors: {}, message: 'Forbidden' }`. A component that calls an action, even from an effect as it mounts, must render inside `app.Wrapper`: outside it the call fails with "called before the page was ready".
- `navigations` records what happened: `{ type: 'push' | 'replace', href }`, `{ type: 'refresh' | 'back' | 'forward' }`, `{ type: 'submit', action, data }` for form posts, `{ type: 'action', name, input }` for action calls.

Render a page component directly with the props its loader would send: `render(<Post title="Hello" body="..." />, { wrapper: createTestApp({ url: '/blog/hello' }).Wrapper })`. A page made with `definePage` parses them with its schema, so props the loader could not send fail the test with `Invalid props: ...`.

For the whole document, as the server sends it (the layouts, the head, Netjes's inline scripts), `renderDocument('app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx', { props, params: { slug: 'hello' }, url: '/blog/hello', layouts: { 'app/blog/layout.tsx': { categories } }, shared })` from `netjes/testing` resolves with the HTML. The test file starts with `// @vitest-environment node`: in a DOM environment it rejects, since the server renders without one. No C# runs, so pass what the loaders would send; a layout that `layouts` does not name gets no props. Nothing else the server adds is there: query entries seeded with `.WithQuery` (a `useQuery` renders without its data), metadata from C#, the antiforgery token, the locale, draft mode, the base path and the image optimiser's settings. A boundary file renders inside the layouts down to its own folder, and `global-error` without any layout, with no route. A Promise in the props is a `Page.Defer` value; pass `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(1000)` when one may never settle. `inlineScriptHashes(html)` is async: `await inlineScriptHashes(html)` resolves to the `'sha256-…'` hashes of the inline scripts in the document that a browser runs, for a Content-Security-Policy without a nonce. With no inline scripts of the app's own they equal `CSP_SCRIPT_HASHES.split(' ')` from `netjes`, as `app/document.test.ts` in a new app checks for the home page: `expect(await inlineScriptHashes(html)).toEqual(CSP_SCRIPT_HASHES.split(' '))`. The document is a crawler's, so React's scripts that reveal a Suspense boundary for a visitor are not in it, nor the inline code of an `afterInteractive` or `lazyOnload` `<Script>`, which the browser adds: its hash goes in the policy only. A `beforeInteractive` `<Script>`'s inline code is in the document, so its hash goes in both.

Fake timers work with Testing Library: after `vi.useFakeTimers()`, create the user with `userEvent.setup({ advanceTimers: vi.advanceTimersByTime })`, and let `findBy…` or `waitFor` wait, which moves the fake clock on (their timeout counts fake time). Run a timer that `fireEvent` started with `await act(() => vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(ms))`, and call `vi.useRealTimers()` in an `afterEach`.

## Loaders and actions: C#

- Loader logic: call the loader or the method it uses and read `PageResult<T>.Props` in an xUnit test.
- Endpoints: test the real app with `WebApplicationFactory<Program>` from `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing` (ASP.NET Core 10 makes the `Program` class of top-level statements public, so the test project sees it). No Node is needed when the test sets `Netjes:Mode` to `Development` (routes come from `app/` on disk) and registers an `ISsrRenderer` (`Netjes.Rendering`) of its own that returns fixed HTML, in `ConfigureServices`. Run it in the `Testing` environment (`builder.UseEnvironment("Testing")`), as the testing guide's factory does: `WebApplicationFactory` uses `Development` unless told otherwise, and there Netjes output-caches no page, so a test of `CachePage` would see every request render. Request a page as the client router does, with the header `X-Netjes-Data: 1` (`NetjesHeaders.Data`): the answer is the page payload as JSON, with `props`, `status` and `antiforgery`; a page with `Page.Defer` values answers NDJSON, the payload first. When the app cannot start (no build in Production, `node` not found), `CreateClient()` throws an `InvalidOperationException` that says why.
- Server actions are `POST /_netjes/actions/{name}`. Call one as the client router does: the fields form-encoded, `X-Netjes-Data: 1`, and the payload's `antiforgery.requestToken` in the header named by `antiforgery.headerName` (a client that keeps cookies, so the antiforgery cookie goes along; `GET /_netjes/antiforgery` returns a token too). A plain form post, as without JavaScript, sends the token as the `antiforgery.formFieldName` field instead.
- Use a real database for data access tests (Testcontainers), not an in-memory fake.

## End to end: Playwright

Put Playwright tests in `e2e/` (Vitest skips it). Run them against the app in Development (`dotnet run --no-launch-profile` with `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development`) and in Production (`npm run build`, then `dotnet run --no-launch-profile` with `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production`), waiting on `/healthz`. Test the forms with JavaScript turned off too (`test.use({ javaScriptEnabled: false })`): they must post, show errors and keep what was typed.

With JavaScript on, wait for hydration after each full page load, before the first click or keystroke; until then links load pages in full and forms post natively, so the test can pass without the client. Netjes puts `data-netjes-hydrated` on `<html>` once the client router runs in the document:

```ts
await page.goto('/');
await expect(page.locator('html')).toHaveAttribute('data-netjes-hydrated', '');
```

`page.locator('html[data-netjes-hydrated]').waitFor({ state: 'attached' })` waits for the same thing without `expect`'s 5-second limit. Never wait on `history.state`: a reload keeps it, so it is there before the page's scripts have run. Content inside a Suspense boundary can hydrate after the mark; React hydrates it first when a click lands on it.

## Before calling a change done

```bash
npm test && npm run typecheck && dotnet build && npx netjes generate --check
```

and `npm run routes` without new warnings.

## More

[Testing](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/guides/testing.md) in the guides, and [`createTestApp`](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/reference/react-api.md#createtestapp) and [`renderDocument`](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/reference/react-api.md#renderdocument) in the React API.

<!-- Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/packages/netjes/skills/netjes/references/deployment.md -->

# Deployment

A Netjes app is an ASP.NET Core app that also needs Node at runtime: the .NET process starts and supervises the Node sidecar that renders pages (`NetjesOptions.NodeExecutable`, default `node` on the `PATH`). Only `netjes export` output runs without either.

## Build and publish

```bash
npx netjes generate --check   # in CI: the generated types match the C# types
npm test && npm run typecheck && dotnet build
dotnet publish -c Release -o bin/publish   # runs `npm run build`, ships dist/ (client, server bundle, sidecar)
cd bin/publish && ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production dotnet MyApp.dll
```

`npx netjes start` runs the app in Production from the source tree (or `--dll bin/publish/MyApp.dll`, which runs from the publish folder). In production the routes come from the built client manifest, so a page file that was not built does not exist.

For these startup failures the app logs one critical entry, saying what is wrong and what to do, and exits with code 1: no build in Production (`npm run build`), a `node` it cannot start (`Netjes:NodeExecutable`), a sidecar script that is not installed or built (`npm install` in development, `npm run build` in production), or in development the Vite dev server's port taken, an error in `vite.config.ts` (with Vite's code frame) or a package it imports that is not installed (`npm install`). Under `WebApplicationFactory` the start throws that message instead. Other exceptions at startup, such as a route conflict, keep their stack. An exception that nothing catches, at startup or on a thread of the app's own, ends it as a .NET crash does: an abort, exit code 134 on Linux and macOS. ASP.NET Core catches a request's exceptions (a page's renders its `error.tsx`), and the host catches one from a `BackgroundService` and stops the app with exit code 0.

## Docker

`netjes new` writes a `Dockerfile` and Compose files:

- `docker compose up`: development, with `dotnet watch` and Vite HMR, ports bound to localhost.
- `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d`: the production image, a non-root user on a read-only filesystem, with a health check on `/healthz` and Data Protection keys in a named volume.
- Both publish the app on host port 8080; `APP_PORT` (in the shell or a `.env` file) moves it. Vite's 5173 stays.
- The production image runs `tini -s -- dotnet MyApp.dll`: tini is PID 1, passes `docker stop`'s SIGTERM on, and exits with the app's code, so a crash ends the container (134) and `restart: always` acts. When .NET itself is a container's PID 1, its abort does not end it. On arm64 it spins at 100% CPU and never exits; after a crash later than startup the rest of the app keeps serving and `/healthz` still passes. On x86-64 under emulation it has been seen to exit after a few seconds, with 139 instead of 134. An image of the app's own, or one from an older template, needs an init too: the template's `tini` stage, its `COPY` and the `ENTRYPOINT`, or the host's (`docker run --init`, Compose `init: true`, ECS `initProcessEnabled`).

The image restores Netjes from NuGet and npm, so the app must reference the packages, as an app made with `npx netjes new` does (from a Netjes checkout, pass `--packages`).

## Production settings

- `AllowedHosts`: pin it to the site's host names. `appsettings.Development.json` already limits Development to loopback names.
- HTTPS: outside Development the template calls `UseHsts()` and `UseHttpsRedirection()`. Behind a proxy that terminates TLS, call `UseForwardedHeaders()` first, trusting only that proxy's network (`KnownIPNetworks`), so the app sees https and the visitor's address.
- Data Protection keys sign antiforgery tokens and draft-mode cookies: keep them across restarts (the production compose file mounts a volume) and share them between instances.
- Several instances behind a load balancer also share the output-cache store and need the same `Netjes:SegmentKeySecret` (32 bytes or more).
- `Netjes:SidecarProcesses`: Node processes rendering in production (default 1; about one per core for CPU-heavy pages).
- If no sidecar is ready (they crashed or stopped answering, and are restarting), documents are sent for the browser to render instead of failing (`ClientRenderFallback`, on by default), and `/healthz` reports Unhealthy. Register the check with `builder.Services.AddHealthChecks().AddNetjes()` and `app.MapHealthChecks("/healthz")`.
- The app restarts its Node processes itself: one that exits, and in production one that answers no health ping within `RenderTimeout` (at least 5 s). A restart policy on the container's exit (`restart: always`) is all the host needs. A custom `Netjes:SidecarScript` must answer `GET /health`, with any status, without reading a request body.
- Output caching: set `SizeLimit`, and see [caching-and-streaming.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/packages/netjes/skills/netjes/references/caching-and-streaming.md).
- Security headers: every response through `UseNetjes()` gets `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, so every response needs its real `Content-Type`: a script or stylesheet with a wrong one or none is refused, and a page that an endpoint writes with `Response.WriteAsync` shows as plain text unless the endpoint sets `Response.ContentType = "text/html; charset=utf-8"` first. Every document also gets `Referrer-Policy` and a same-origin framing policy, or the `X-Frame-Options` that the policy's `frame-ancestors` implies, unless the app sets them (`Netjes:SecurityHeaders`). A Content-Security-Policy is off until you set `NetjesOptions.ContentSecurityPolicy`: with `{nonce}` for a nonce-based policy, or without it, with `NetjesContentSecurityPolicy.ScriptHashes` in its `script-src`, for a hash-based one, which output-cached pages need ([caching-and-streaming.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/packages/netjes/skills/netjes/references/caching-and-streaming.md)).
- `Netjes:PublicConfig` is sent to the browser as is; secrets go in other configuration.
- Telemetry: add the `Netjes` ActivitySource and Meter (`NetjesTelemetry.Name`) to OpenTelemetry for loader, action and render spans and render durations.

## Startup work and CLI commands

`netjes generate` and `netjes routes` run the app once in command mode, without serving or starting Node. Skip startup work they do not need, such as migrations or seeding:

```csharp
if (app.GetNetjesCommand() is null)
{
    await SeedAsync(app.Services);
}
```

## Static hosting

`npx netjes export` writes the site as static HTML to `out/` for any static host; see [caching-and-streaming.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/packages/netjes/skills/netjes/references/caching-and-streaming.md#static-export) for what it needs and refuses.

## More

[Deployment](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/guides/deployment.md) and [Security](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/guides/security.md) in the guides, and every option in [Options](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/reference/options.md).

<!-- Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/README.md -->

# Design decisions

These records explain why Netjes is built the way it is, for contributors and for anyone weighing it against another framework. Each one states a decision, the context that led to it, the alternatives considered and what follows from it. [The architecture page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/architecture.md) describes how the pieces fit together; these records say why they are those pieces.

- [0001 – React renders in a pool of Node sidecars](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0001-react-renders-in-node-sidecars.md): supervised Node processes render React, and .NET balances renders between them.
- [0002 – The server owns routing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0002-server-owns-routing.md): routes are matched in C# only, and the client router asks the server for every page.
- [0003 – React renders the whole document](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0003-react-renders-the-whole-document.md): React renders `<html>` itself, head and metadata included.
- [0004 – Vite for the dev server and builds](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0004-vite-for-dev-server-and-builds.md): Vite serves modules in development and builds the client and server bundles.
- [0005 – A small default stack](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0005-a-small-default-stack.md): React, TanStack Query, Tailwind CSS and Vitest, with no other runtime dependencies.
- [0006 – Types and zod schemas generated from the C# contracts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0006-types-and-zod-from-csharp-contracts.md): the running app writes `generated/netjes.ts` from its System.Text.Json contracts.
- [0007 – A Node CLI in the npm package, which asks the app itself](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0007-a-node-cli-that-asks-the-app.md): `netjes` runs the app in command mode to report its routes and types.
- [0008 – Image processing is pluggable, SkiaSharp optional](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0008-pluggable-image-processing.md): the image endpoint owns the rules, and a separate package resizes.
- [0009 – Public configuration is sent at runtime](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0009-public-config-at-runtime.md): `Netjes:PublicConfig` reaches the browser with the first document, not through the build.
- [0010 – The App Router's conventions, with C# layout loaders instead of server components](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0010-app-router-with-csharp-layout-loaders.md): `app/` only, and each segment's data comes from C#.
- [0011 – Server actions are C# endpoints with typed references](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0011-server-actions-as-csharp-endpoints.md): stable names, antiforgery and origin checks, and forms that work without JavaScript.
- [0012 – Streamed documents, deferred values, and ready boundaries in place](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0012-streamed-documents-and-deferred-values.md): documents stream, `Page.Defer` values follow the shell, and ready boundaries need no script.
- [0013 – A client-rendered fallback when no sidecar is ready](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0013-client-rendered-fallback.md): .NET sends the payload for the browser to render while Node is down.
- [0014 – Signing in or out clears what Back shows](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0014-signing-in-or-out-clears-what-back-shows.md): a cookie change in an action makes the router and the browser forget pages.
- [0015 – Route warnings name what is likely wrong, not everything that could be](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0015-route-warnings-name-what-is-likely-wrong.md): startup warnings for query-bound loader parameters and overlapping pages.
- [0016 – Page cache rules under any output caching](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0016-page-cache-rules-under-any-output-caching.md): page keys, tags and token rules apply whatever policy caches a page.
- [0017 – A form input without any of its fields is empty, not null](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0017-a-form-input-without-fields-is-empty-not-null.md): an action gets an empty `[FromForm]` input, checked like any other, where form binding gives none.
- [0018 – A startup failure that says what to do ends the app in one line](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0018-startup-failures-end-in-one-line.md): a missing build, Node.js or Vite dev server is one log entry and exit code 1, and a failed start in a test host.
- [0019 – A forced no-store removes the headers CDNs read first](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0019-forced-no-store-removes-cdn-cache-headers.md): drafts, the fallback and the other `no-store` responses go out without `CDN-Cache-Control`, `Surrogate-Control` and the like.
- [0020 – Page actions check their inputs like server actions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0020-page-actions-check-their-inputs-like-server-actions.md): a failed check renders the page again from its loader, and `usePageActionState()` reads it.
- [0021 – Signing in or out reaches the app's other tabs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0021-signing-in-or-out-reaches-the-other-tabs.md): a tab that sees a cookie change tells the others on a `BroadcastChannel`, and they forget and reload the same way.
- [0022 – The client entry hydrates once the shell is parsed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0022-hydrate-once-the-shell-is-parsed.md): it waits for the empty element that ends every document's body, so a cached entry never hydrates half a document.
- [0023 – Pages are not output-cached in Development](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0023-pages-are-not-output-cached-in-development.md): there every request renders the page, nothing is stored, and the page goes out `no-store`, so no edit meets a stale document.
- [0024 – Link marks the current page by its path and the query parameters it names](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0024-link-marks-the-current-page-by-path-and-query.md): `aria-current="page"` goes on a link to the page on screen, never on a `#` link, and query parameters the link does not name do not count.
- [0025 – A mark on `<html>` says the client router runs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0025-a-mark-on-html-says-the-client-router-runs.md): `data-netjes-hydrated` appears once the router is the page's action client, in every document, and end-to-end tests wait for it rather than for `history.state`.
- [0026 – Netjes's own `<html>` and `<body>` skip React's attribute check](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0026-netjes-html-and-body-skip-reacts-attribute-check.md): a script that sets an attribute on either one before hydration, such as a theme script or a browser extension, no longer makes React log a mismatch in development.
- [0027 – Testing Library advances Vitest's fake timers through a jest global that exists only while they are on](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0027-testing-library-advances-vitest-fake-timers.md): a setup file the plugin adds to every app's tests bridges `jest.advanceTimersByTime` to Vitest while its timers are fake, so `waitFor`, `findBy` and user-event return.
- [0028 – The test harness starts from the app's query defaults and keeps its retries, without the waits](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0028-test-harness-starts-from-the-apps-query-defaults.md): `createTestApp` layers the app's `netjes({ query })` defaults, which the plugin provides to the tests, under its own `retryDelay: 0`.
- [0029 – An endpoint that ties with a page is a route warning](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0029-an-endpoint-that-ties-with-a-page-is-a-route-warning.md): an endpoint of the app that ranks the same as a page or a page action, which ASP.NET Core answers with 500 for the URLs both match, is warned about at startup and in `netjes routes`.
- [0030 – Security headers beyond documents](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0030-security-headers-beyond-documents.md): `nosniff` goes on every response through `UseNetjes`, and documents carry the `X-Frame-Options` their `frame-ancestors` implies, set before antiforgery could add its own.
- [0031 – A sidecar that stops answering is restarted like one that crashed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0031-a-sidecar-that-stops-answering-is-restarted.md): in production a Node process silent for five seconds is pinged, and killed and restarted when no answer comes within `RenderTimeout`.
- [0032 – The release links the package READMEs to its tag](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0032-release-links-package-readmes-to-its-tag.md): the READMEs link the docs on `main`, and the release job moves those links to `v<version>` in the packages it publishes, so npm and NuGet show each version with links to its own docs.
- [0033 – Client navigations announce the page and start the focus over](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0033-client-navigations-announce-the-page-and-start-the-focus-over.md): a polite live region names the new page, and the focus starts over at the top of the document or goes to a fragment's element; it stays on the same page, where the page or the user moved it, and in a field or on a `scroll={false}` link that still has it.
- [0034 – Navigation promises resolve when React has the page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0034-navigation-promises-resolve-when-react-has-the-page.md): `router.push`, `replace` and `refresh` resolve once the router has handed the page to React, not once React has committed it, which inside a form action would never happen.
- [0035 – Development styles are inlined from the client environment's build](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0035-development-styles-are-inlined-from-the-client-build.md): the sidecar inlines the CSS text that the browser's module for each file sets, so Vite's client changes nothing before hydration, and React no longer checks the text of those elements.
- [0036 – zod runs without compiled parsers in the browser](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0036-zod-runs-without-compiled-parsers-in-the-browser.md): the client entry's first import sets zod's `jitless`, so no policy without `'unsafe-eval'` reports zod's test for `new Function`, and the sidecar and Vitest keep the compiled parsers.
- [0037 – Netjes keeps an app's Content-Security-Policy as written in Development, and warns](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0037-csp-kept-as-written-in-development-with-warnings.md): the policy goes out as written in every mode, and Netjes warns once per policy when it refuses the bootstrap or the module scripts, holds a nonce that is not the document's, or in Development refuses the Vite dev server's scripts, its socket or the inlined styles.
- [0038 – `netjes/testing` renders a page's document from its props](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0038-netjes-testing-renders-a-pages-document.md): `renderDocument` builds the payload from the pages map by the server's rules, which a fixture shared with the C# tests keeps the same, instead of `netjes/server-entry` and its payload becoming public.
- [0039 – A page URL has one spelling](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0039-a-page-url-has-one-spelling.md): a `GET` or `HEAD` for a page in another case of its literal segments, and with `TrailingSlash.Never` one with a trailing slash, answers 308 with the file's spelling, built from the URL the client sent.
- [0040 – Links from C# are a Href type](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0040-links-from-csharp-are-a-href-type.md): a `Netjes.Href` in props is checked for its shape in C# and generated as the `Href` schema, which checks it against the app's pages where the props are parsed, so a component passes it to `<Link>` as it is.
- [0041 – The export warns about loaders that read the query string](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0041-the-export-warns-about-loaders-that-read-the-query-string.md): a static host serves an exported page's file for every query string, so `netjes export` logs a warning for each such loader, in `Netjes.Export.QueryString`, and still writes the page.
- [0042 – The app's image runs an init as PID 1, so a crash ends the container](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0042-the-apps-image-runs-an-init-as-pid-1.md): the template's and the examples' production images start the app with `tini -s --`, so a crash ends the container with code 134 and `docker stop` reaches the app, where .NET as PID 1 spun or exited with another code.
- [0043 – Netjes marks the errors whose message it withheld](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0043-netjes-marks-the-errors-whose-message-it-withheld.md): `error.withheld` is true on an error whose message Netjes wrote in place of one it does not show, so an error page renders the message only when `!error.withheld`, and the router's top-level boundary hands the app's error page the error it caught.
- [0044 – `beforeInteractive` scripts run before the page's code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0044-before-interactive-scripts-run-before-the-pages-code.md): inline code runs where it stands, before what follows it is painted, and external scripts run in order once the shell is parsed, before the page's modules run and the page hydrates.
- [0045 – Typed URLs for the app's endpoints](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0045-typed-urls-for-the-apps-endpoints.md): the generated `endpointUrl()` builds the URL of the app's endpoints that are not pages or actions, by a key written as in `api`, its method and route (a JSON endpoint one for each method but `HEAD`, any other one for `GET` if it answers `GET`), with the route values and query values its handler binds typed in TypeScript as binding accepts them, and without the base path, which `useHref` adds.
- [0046 – The export writes the GET endpoints marked IncludeInExport](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0046-the-export-writes-the-get-endpoints-marked-includeinexport.md): `netjes export` writes the answer of each endpoint marked `.IncludeInExport()` as a file at its URL, `MapSitemap` and `MapRobotsTxt` among them, and the exported sitemap lists the pages the export writes.

A decision that a newcomer would not guess, or that was chosen over a real alternative, gets a new record with the next number. An accepted record is not rewritten when the decision changes; a new record supersedes it.

<!-- Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/CHANGELOG.md -->

# Changelog

All notable changes to Netjes are recorded here: the `netjes` npm package and the `Netjes` and `Netjes.Images.SkiaSharp` NuGet packages, which are released together under one version. The format follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and versions follow [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html). Before 1.0, a new version can change the API; its entry says what to do.

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- `<Link>`, `<Form>`, `<SubmitButton>` and `<Image>` take a `ref` to the element they render. `LinkProps`, `FormProps`, `SubmitButtonProps` and `ImageProps` now start from React's `ComponentPropsWithRef` instead of the `*HTMLAttributes` types, which left the ref out, so `<Link ref={ref}>` is no longer a type error. The ref already reached the element at runtime, and only the types refused it; an app that worked around the type error, for example with `document.getElementById(id)`, can pass the ref instead. The four types also include `key` now; React handles it, as for any element, and never passes it to the component.
- Once the client router runs in a document, `<html>` carries `data-netjes-hydrated=""`: the sign that the client router runs in the document, which end-to-end tests wait for before they click, with `await expect(page.locator('html')).toHaveAttribute('data-netjes-hydrated', '')` ([testing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/testing.md#wait-for-hydration), [ADR 0025](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0025-a-mark-on-html-says-the-client-router-runs.md)). Content inside a Suspense boundary can hydrate after it. It appears after the router has registered as the page's action client, on hydrated pages and on pages rendered in the browser when no sidecar was ready, and the server never renders it. A test helper that waited for the router's key in `history.state` should wait for the attribute instead: the browser keeps that state when it loads the document again, so after a reload the key is there before any of the page's scripts has run. The name is reserved, and a stylesheet or a DOM snapshot that reads `<html>`'s attributes in the browser now sees one more.
- Testing Library works with Vitest's fake timers. Under `vi.useFakeTimers()`, `waitFor`, `findBy…` and user-event never returned, because Testing Library moves fake timers on only through Jest's `jest` global. Netjes's setup file now defines that global while Vitest's timers are fake, and leaves it undefined with real timers ([ADR 0027](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0027-testing-library-advances-vitest-fake-timers.md)). `waitFor` and `findBy…` move the fake clock on as they wait, and their timeout counts fake time; create user-event's user with `userEvent.setup({ advanceTimers: vi.advanceTimersByTime })`. While timers are fake, `typeof jest` is `'object'`, so a library that looks for Jest finds it then, and a test on `vi.useFakeTimers({ shouldAdvanceTime: true })` takes Testing Library's path for fake timers. A `jest` global the app's own setup file defines, or a test assigns, is kept.
- `createTestApp()` starts from the app's `netjes({ query })` defaults. `netjes()` sets Vitest's `test.provide['netjes:query']` to the `query` option's `defaultOptions` (`{}` when there are none, nothing with `query: false`), next to the app's own `provide` keys, and Netjes's setup file hands them to the harness ([ADR 0028](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0028-test-harness-starts-from-the-apps-query-defaults.md)).
- A route warning for an endpoint of the app that ties with a page or a page action. Such an endpoint ranks the same as the page in ASP.NET Core's matcher: it has an HTTP method in common with it, the same order, route precedence and literals, a host in common or no host on either, and accepted content types listed by both or by neither (two endpoints that both list content types tie for a request without one, such as a POST without a body). ASP.NET Core cannot choose between the two and answers each request that both match with 500 (`AmbiguousMatchException`), as it did before. Now the app also logs a warning at startup, in the category `Netjes.Routing.RouteDiagnostics`, and `netjes routes` lists it (the kind `ambiguous-endpoint` in `--json`), naming the endpoint's methods and route and the page file. Netjes's own `MapLocaleRedirect()` next to an `app/page.tsx` is one such endpoint. Give the endpoint `.WithOrder(-1)` if it should answer those URLs, or change its route. An app that keeps the tie, or whose own matcher policies tell the two endpoints apart, can raise the category's log level, which hides every route warning ([ADR 0029](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0029-an-endpoint-that-ties-with-a-page-is-a-route-warning.md)). The routing guide has a new section, [Endpoints next to pages](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/routing.md#endpoints-next-to-pages), on which endpoint answers a URL and how to link to a file next to a page.
- `PageRouteMetadata` and `CachedPageMetadata` in `Netjes.Routing`, so app code and tests can find the app's pages by walking `EndpointDataSource`, as `netjes routes` does ([endpoint metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/reference/csharp-api.md#endpoint-metadata)). Every endpoint that serves a page carries `PageRouteMetadata`, with the page's `Pattern` as its file names it and `IsLoader`, true on the endpoint `MapPageLoader` maps. Every endpoint `CachePage` is put on carries `CachedPageMetadata`, with the `Duration` and `Tags` it was given. Apart from `CachePage`'s copy of its tags (under Changed), this is new API only, and nothing else changes at runtime. Code that finds a page's endpoint by its display name (`Page /blog/[slug]`), which is not part of the API, can read `PageRouteMetadata` instead.
- `route()` and `buildHref` take a fourth argument, `{ hash }`, which adds a `#fragment` after the query: `route('/docs/[...path]', { path: ['guides', 'caching'] }, undefined, { hash: 'keys' })` is `/docs/guides/caching#keys`. The hash is the id of an element on the page. One leading `#` is dropped and the rest is percent-encoded (`'über-uns'` becomes `#%C3%BCber-uns`, which browsers and the router decode when they look for the element); with nothing left, no fragment is added. The third argument is still the query, so a link with a fragment and no query passes `undefined` there ([routing guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/routing.md#links)). The generated `route()` has a new signature, so run `npx netjes generate` after upgrading, or start the app in Development, and commit `generated/netjes.ts`: `npx netjes generate --check` in CI fails until you do. Until then `route()` keeps its old signature and takes no `hash`. A link whose fragment you write into the string yourself needs no change.
- `NetjesContentSecurityPolicy.ScriptHashes` in C# and `CSP_SCRIPT_HASHES` from `netjes` hold the `script-src` sources that allow, by their hashes, the inline scripts Netjes writes with the same text into every document, for a Content-Security-Policy without a nonce: `$"script-src 'self' {NetjesContentSecurityPolicy.ScriptHashes}; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'"` ([security](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/security.md#hash-based)). In this version they hold one hash, of the bootstrap that collects streamed `Page.Defer` values: `'sha256-FSjVV+FzmXP8KKrLKLdvst/5N/bEWSkde01XzpGKRgs='`, the hash the docs gave for apps to paste, unchanged since 0.0.1. An app that pasted it into its policy replaces it with the constant. Nothing changes in this version, but a pasted hash blocks the bootstrap once a Netjes version changes the script, while the constants change with it. The scripts that deliver `Page.Defer` values, and React's scripts that reveal Suspense boundaries, are still covered by no hash. Nor do the constants hold the hash of React's script for form actions that are functions, whose text follows the React version; the security guide says what a page with such an action needs.
- After a client navigation to another path or query, the router announces the new page in a visually hidden live region (`aria-live="polite"`, marked `data-netjes-route-announcer`), which it renders after the app's content once the page has hydrated. It reads the page's `document.title`, else the text of its first `h1`, else its path, and speaks only when that differs from the previous page's name. A refresh, a form post that stays on its page, a link to a fragment of the page on screen and a page that an intercepting route shows in a modal are not announced ([Focus and announcements](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/routing.md#focus-and-announcements), [ADR 0033](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0033-client-navigations-announce-the-page-and-start-the-focus-over.md)). The server's HTML does not change, and the region has no role, so a test's `getByRole('status')` or `getByRole('alert')` finds what it found before. Give each page a title of its own: a page whose title is the previous page's is not announced. Remove an announcer of the app's own, or each page is announced twice. An end-to-end test that reads the whole text of a container, such as `body`, now also gets the region's text: read the element it means instead.
- New apps' root layout starts with a "Skip to content" link to `<main id="content">`, the first element Tab reaches after a page load and, now that the router starts the focus over, after a client navigation. An existing app can add the same to its root layout: `<Link href="#content" prefetch="none" className="sr-only focus:not-sr-only">Skip to content</Link>` first, and `id="content"` on its `<main>`.
- Warnings when a document's Content-Security-Policy refuses what the document needs. Netjes compares each policy in the `Content-Security-Policy` header that goes out on a document, the app's own or else `NetjesOptions.ContentSecurityPolicy`, with what the document needs, and `Netjes.Rendering.PageRenderer` logs a warning for each problem, once per policy, naming the directive and what to change. Scripts follow `script-src-elem`, else `script-src`, else `default-src`, and a list there that holds the document's nonce allows them all. For any other list, Netjes warns when the list refuses the inline bootstrap (it lists neither the hashes in `NetjesContentSecurityPolicy.ScriptHashes` nor `'unsafe-inline'` without a hash, a nonce or `'strict-dynamic'` beside it), has `'strict-dynamic'`, or holds none of `'self'`, `*`, `http:`, `https:` or a host source for the module scripts; when such a list holds a nonce that is not the document's, one the app made without `HttpContext.GetCspNonce()`, the one warning for it says to take the nonce from `GetCspNonce()`. In Development it also warns when such a list leaves out the Vite dev server's origin (`http://localhost:5173` by default), when `connect-src`, or `default-src` without `connect-src`, leaves out the HMR socket (`ws://localhost:5173`, which neither `'self'` nor a nonce covers), and when the list that style elements follow (`style-src-elem`, else `style-src`, else `default-src`) holds neither the document's nonce nor `'unsafe-inline'` without a hash or nonce beside it, for the styles Netjes inlines and Vite's client adds. It does not check the images and fonts that Vite serves from its origin in Development, which a policy with `img-src`, `font-src` or `default-src` lists there ([what Netjes checks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/security.md#what-netjes-checks), [in development](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/security.md#in-development), [ADR 0037](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0037-csp-kept-as-written-in-development-with-warnings.md)). The policy still goes out as written, in Development too, and nothing else changes. An app that sees such a warning changes its policy as the warning says, and in Development it can instead send the policy only outside Development; an app that sees none has nothing to do.
- `renderDocument(page, options)` and `inlineScriptHashes(html)` in `netjes/testing`, with the type `RenderDocumentOptions` for the options. `renderDocument` renders a page's whole document as the server sends it to a crawler, the page inside its layouts with the head, Netjes's inline scripts and the payload, from what the test passes: the props, each layout's props by the layout's file, the shared props, the route values and the URL ([the document](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/testing.md#the-document), [ADR 0038](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0038-netjes-testing-renders-a-pages-document.md)). A Promise in the props is a `Page.Defer` value. It builds the segments that wrap the page from the pages map, by the server's rules, and leaves out what only the server adds: the build's stylesheets and scripts, development styles, the query entries a loader seeds with `.WithQuery`, metadata from C#, the antiforgery token, the locale, draft mode, the base path and the image optimiser's settings. A boundary file renders inside the layouts down to its own folder, and `global-error` without any layout, with no route. It runs in Vitest's node environment, with the `netjes()` plugin: a test file that calls it starts with `// @vitest-environment node`, and in a DOM environment it rejects with an error that says so. `inlineScriptHashes` lists the `'sha256-…'` hashes of the inline scripts in a document that a browser runs, to compare with those a policy without a nonce lists; a crawler's document has none of the scripts React streams to reveal a Suspense boundary for a visitor, and no code of an `afterInteractive` or `lazyOnload` `<Script>`, which the browser adds. New apps get `app/document.test.ts`, which renders the home page's document and checks that the only inline script in it is the one `CSP_SCRIPT_HASHES` lists; an existing app can copy it from the template. A test that renders a document through `netjes/server-entry`, with a payload it writes itself, can call `renderDocument` instead: that entry point and its payload stay internal and can change in any version. The plugin's `virtual:netjes/pages` module now also exports `appDir`. Apps that call neither function have nothing to change.
- `NetjesOptions.TrailingSlash` (`Netjes:TrailingSlash`) and the enum `TrailingSlash` decide whether a page's URL may end in a slash. `Ignore`, the default, answers `/about` and `/about/` alike, as before. `Never` answers a `GET` or `HEAD` for `/about/` with a 308 to `/about`, and a client navigation with a redirect payload; a catch-all's value loses its last slash (`/docs/a/b/` goes to `/docs/a/b`, so `[...path]` gets `a/b`), and `/` stays as it is, also under a base path. `/robots.txt/` and `/sitemap.xml/` go to `/robots.txt` and `/sitemap.xml` too. Only the URL the client sent is redirected, as for another case of a page's URL (below). Behind a proxy or CDN that adds a trailing slash, `Never` loops: turn off one of the two ([One URL per page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/routing.md#one-url-per-page), [ADR 0039](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0039-a-page-url-has-one-spelling.md)). Its sibling, `NetjesOptions.RedirectLiteralCase` (`Netjes:RedirectLiteralCase`, true by default), turns off the case redirect described under Changed.
- `Netjes.Href`, for a link that C# sends to one of the app's pages or to another site: `public sealed record NavLink(Href Href, string Label)`, filled with `new Href("/about")`. The generated file writes a property of that type as its `Href` schema (`Href.nullable()`, `z.array(Href)` and so on), so the props parse checks the link against the app's pages, and a component passes it to `<Link href>` without `Href.parse` or a cast ([Links from C#](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/data-loading.md#links-from-c), [ADR 0040](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0040-links-from-csharp-are-a-href-type.md)). The constructor throws `ArgumentException`, and `Href.TryCreate` returns false, for a URL that starts with none of `/`, `?`, `#`, `http:`, `https:`, `mailto:` and `tel:`, that starts with `//` or `/\`, that holds an ASCII control character, or that starts or ends with a space. C# checks only that shape: a root-relative `Href` that no page serves, such as `/llms.txt` or a URL that already has the base path, fails the props parse, and the page renders its nearest error boundary. The server answers that with 500 when the component that parses the link is outside every Suspense boundary; under one, such as a `loading.tsx`, it sends the boundary's fallback with the loader's status, and the error boundary renders in the browser. So a link to an endpoint or a file stays a `string`, and so does a link from a CMS, checked with `isHref` where it is rendered. JSON holds an `Href` as a plain string, written by `HrefJsonConverter`, which is public so that a source-generated `JsonSerializerContext` can use it too. Minimal APIs bind no query value, route value or header to it, `[AsParameters]` included, and form binding reads none from the field of a property's name, so a URL from the request, such as a `returnUrl`, stays a `string`. Form binding can still build one from a field named after the constructor's parameter (`next.url` for a property `Next`), checked for its shape only, so keep `Href` out of `[FromForm]` inputs, which take a `string`. Props of type `string` are unchanged, and an app that sends no `Href` has nothing to do but regenerate: the generated file now declares `routePatterns`, `isHref()` and the `Href` schema right after its imports, before the schemas of the C# types, which may use it, and its exports are the same. Run `npx netjes generate` after upgrading, or start the app in Development, and commit `generated/netjes.ts`: `npx netjes generate --check` in CI fails until you do.
- `netjes export` warns about each loader that reads the query string: a page loader of a page it writes, or a layout loader above one. The export requests every URL without a query string, and a static host serves the file it wrote for every query string, so such a page shows what its loader returned without one, whatever the address holds: `/blog?tag=react` gets the page written for `/blog`. The page is still written and the exit code is unchanged. A loader that requires the value, through a parameter with no default value and a type that is not nullable (`int page`, or `string q` with nullable reference types on), still fails the export, as before: minimal APIs answer 400 without the value, and the pages below a layout loader that requires one fail. Its warning names the keys it requires and says that the export fails; give the parameter a default value or a nullable type to export the page without one. The warning, in the new category `Netjes.Export.QueryString`, names the file, the query string keys, and the page's route or the pages below the layout ([static export](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/static-export.md#loaders-that-read-the-query-string), [ADR 0041](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0041-the-export-warns-about-loaders-that-read-the-query-string.md)). A parameter counts when minimal API binding reads it from the query string, `[FromQuery]` and members of an `[AsParameters]` type included; a loader that reads `HttpContext.Request.Query` itself, or takes a type that binds itself with `BindAsync`, is not reported. To act on it, make the value a route parameter with `.StaticParams(...)` to export a page for each value, or exclude the page with `.ExcludeFromExport()` (on a layout loader, it leaves out every page below the layout). For a page meant to be exported without its query string, set `Logging:LogLevel:Netjes.Export.QueryString` to `Error`, which silences the warning for every loader. The Blog example's export now logs one, for `/blog`, whose tag filter it keeps as its example. The docs now also say that `useSearchParams()` sees no query string on an exported page, whatever the address bar shows, and show `window.location.search` read in an effect as the remedy ([in the browser](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/static-export.md#in-the-browser)).
- `APP_PORT` moves the host port of the template's Compose stacks. `APP_PORT=8090 docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d` publishes the production app on port 8090, and `APP_PORT=8090 docker compose up` publishes development on 127.0.0.1:8090; without it, both publish port 8080 as before. Compose reads it from the shell or from a `.env` file next to the Compose files. The app still listens on 8080 inside the container, and Vite's port, 5173, does not move ([Docker](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/deployment.md#docker)). An app made before this release that wants it changes `"8080:8080"` in its `docker-compose.prod.yml` to `"${APP_PORT:-8080}:8080"`, and `"127.0.0.1:8080:8080"` in its `docker-compose.override.yml` to `"127.0.0.1:${APP_PORT:-8080}:8080"`.
- `error.withheld` and `ServerActionError.withheld` mark an error whose message Netjes wrote in place of one it does not show: the error an `error.tsx` gets for an exception the server rendered the page for with error details off (`IncludeErrorDetails`, off outside the Development environment), whose message is the status's reason phrase; a `Page.Defer` value whose failure the server sent without its message; a server action call whose answer had no message, as for a 5xx with error details off; and a thrown value that is neither an Error nor a string. `ErrorPageProps` types it as `withheld?: boolean`. A status rendered without an exception, such as `Page.Forbidden()` where no `forbidden.tsx` is, keeps its reason phrase and is not withheld. The template's and the examples' error pages render `error.message` only when `!error.withheld`, so in production they no longer print "Internal Server Error" under their heading. An app's error page that renders `error.message` works as before; to leave the stand-in out, render the message only when `!error.withheld` ([`ErrorPageProps`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/reference/react-api.md#errorpageprops), [ADR 0043](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0043-netjes-marks-the-errors-whose-message-it-withheld.md)).
- A failure from `createTestApp()`'s `actions` can carry `message`, the message the server would send: `{ ok: false, status: 403, errors: {}, message: 'Forbidden' }`. Without one, a failure other than a 422 throws a `ServerActionError` with `withheld` true, whatever its status, as for a 5xx with error details off. A test that fakes a refused call and expects its error page to show the reason adds the `message` ([Answering server actions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/testing.md#answering-server-actions)).
- Typed URLs for the app's endpoints: `endpointUrl()`, `EndpointParams` and `EndpointKey` in the generated file, and `buildEndpointUrl` in `netjes`, which `endpointUrl()` calls. The endpoints the app maps have keys, their method and route as in `api` (`'GET /api/posts/{slug}/likes/'`), JSON or not: a JSON endpoint one for each of its methods except `HEAD`, any other endpoint one for `GET`, if it answers `GET`. Pages, page actions, server actions, endpoints that name no HTTP method, fallbacks, static assets and MVC conventional routes have none. `endpointUrl(key, params, search)` fills the route with the encoded values and puts the query values the handler binds, then those of `search`, in the query string. The route values and query values are typed from the C# handler, an enum as its C# names and its values, which the query string binds; a missing required route value and a name the endpoint does not bind are type errors. The URL has no base path: pass it through `useHref` for a `fetch` or an `<a href>`, where a hand-built `/api/...` URL misses the base path under `UsePathBase`. Run `npx netjes generate` after upgrading: every app's generated file changes, and imports `buildEndpointUrl` from `netjes`. A C# type named `EndpointParams`, `EndpointKey`, `endpointTemplates`, `endpointUrl` or `buildEndpointUrl` gets a qualified schema name, with its declaring type or its namespace (`MyAppFeaturesEndpointParams` for `MyApp.Features.EndpointParams`): change the app's imports of that schema. The generated file now holds the route of each such endpoint, an endpoint mapped only in Development included. Once any component calls `endpointUrl`, all of them reach the browser in the chunk that holds the file, which pages share, also those that never call it. A route in the file is no easier to reach than one outside it: keep authorization on the endpoint (`RequireAuthorization()`), and do not rely on a URL staying unknown ([security](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/security.md#errors-and-configuration)). Netjes's own endpoints (`/_netjes/image`, `/_netjes/antiforgery`, the vitals beacon and the locale redirect) have no key, and answer as before ([Endpoint URLs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/data-loading.md#endpoint-urls), [ADR 0045](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0045-typed-urls-for-the-apps-endpoints.md)).
- `netjes export` writes `sitemap.xml` and `robots.txt` for an app that maps `MapSitemap` and `MapRobotsTxt`, requested from the app after the pages like a page. The exported sitemap lists the pages the export writes, in the order it writes them, and leaves out the pages marked `.ExcludeFromSitemap()` or `.ExcludeFromExport()`; the sitemap the app serves lists the pages marked `.ExcludeFromExport()` as before. Both files take their URLs from the `siteUrl` passed to the Map calls in the Production environment, which the export runs in. To keep either file out, add `.ExcludeFromExport()` to its Map call, and to `MapRobotsTxt` as well when the sitemap is left out, since `robots.txt` names it. A check that expects the export to hold neither file must change ([static export](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/static-export.md#sitemap-and-robotstxt), [ADR 0046](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0046-the-export-writes-the-get-endpoints-marked-includeinexport.md)).
- `.IncludeInExport()`, a convention for an endpoint that is no page (on a page's loader or `MapPages()` it changes nothing), which `netjes export` writes as a file at its URL, like a Next.js route handler with `dynamic = 'force-static'`: `app.MapGet("/llms.txt", ...).IncludeInExport()` writes `out/llms.txt`. The export requests it with a `GET` and no query string after the pages and writes the body of its 200 byte for byte, without its headers; any other status fails the export. It fails before writing anything when such an endpoint answers no `GET`, has route parameters, a path segment that is no safe file name or a last segment without a file extension, requires authorization, or has the path of a file in the client build or of another file the export writes. `.ExcludeFromExport()` wins over it. One that reads the query string is warned about in `Netjes.Export.QueryString`, as a page loader is ([static export](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/static-export.md#other-endpoints-as-files-includeinexport)).

### Changed

- `netjes()` adds a setup file of its own to every app's Vitest `setupFiles`, after the app's own setup files, also when the app sets `setupFiles` itself, `[]` included. The cleanup file (`netjes/testing/setup`) is still added only when the app sets none. An app that set `setupFiles: []` to keep Netjes's setup files out now gets the new one; `netjes({ test: false })` still leaves out every Vitest setting the plugin adds, this file included. Under Vitest 5, an inline project in `test.projects` that shares the Vite server of the config declaring it, Vitest's default, gets neither this file nor the plugin's defaults (jsdom, `exclude`, cleanup): set `sharedViteServer: false` in the root's `test` options.
- In `createTestApp()` tests, a failed query or mutation is tried as often as in the app, with no wait between the tries; retries used to be off. A query that fails once and then succeeds now shows its data, and an error shows once the last try has failed. A test that expects the error after the first request passes `defaultOptions: { queries: { retry: false } }`, the old behaviour, and `mutations: { retry: false }` where the app's `netjes({ query })` retries mutations. The app's `staleTime`, `retry`, refetch options and mutation `retry` now apply in its tests, and its `retryDelay` and its queries' `gcTime` do not. Seeded queries now stay fresh for the app's `staleTime`, counted from when `createTestApp()` is called, instead of one minute. With an app `staleTime` of 0, a component fetches its seeded query again as it mounts, as in the browser; with another one below a minute, only a component that mounts after that time, such as one rendered after the test moved fake timers on. Answer that request, or pass `defaultOptions: { queries: { staleTime: 60_000 } }`.
- Pages are no longer output-cached in the Development environment. Under `CachePage` or any other output caching, every request there renders the page, nothing is stored, and an output-cached page goes out `Cache-Control: no-store, private` unless it sets its own header. A stored page used to outlive every edit, and its markup and styles no longer matched the code, so React reported a hydration error ([ADR 0023](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0023-pages-are-not-output-cached-in-development.md)). Production and every other environment are unchanged, and `netjes routes` still lists `CachePage` pages as cached. A `WebApplicationFactory` test that checks page caching in the Development environment now sees every request render: run it with `UseEnvironment("Testing")` and `Netjes:Mode` set to `Development`. An app that kept `UseOutputCache()` out of Development can drop that guard; to keep data that is slow or costly to load from loading on every request there, cache it in the service that loads it (`IMemoryCache`, `HybridCache`). In Development the cookie warning now says that outside Development the render is stored, and `Netjes.Rendering.PageCachePolicy` logs once, at Information, that pages are not output-cached there.
- `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` now goes on every response that passes through `UseNetjes()`, not only on documents and images: client payloads, static files from `public/` and the client build, `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml`, `/_netjes/antiforgery`, the app's own endpoints and answers from the output cache. A value the app sets itself is kept. A browser now refuses to run a script, or apply a stylesheet, served with no `Content-Type` or with one that is not a JavaScript type or `text/css`, and no longer takes a response with no `Content-Type` for HTML: it shows the markup as plain text and runs none of its scripts. Serve such responses with the right type; an endpoint that writes a page itself with `Response.WriteAsync` sets `Response.ContentType = "text/html; charset=utf-8"` first. Responses that middleware registered before `UseNetjes()` writes itself still go without it. `Netjes:SecurityHeaders:Enabled` set to false turns it off, and the image endpoint keeps its own `nosniff` either way ([ADR 0030](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0030-security-headers-beyond-documents.md)).
- With `frame-ancestors` in the Content-Security-Policy that goes out, documents now carry the `X-Frame-Options` it implies: `DENY` for `'none'`, an empty list or other sites only, and `SAMEORIGIN` when the list holds `'self'`, `*` or a scheme source such as `https:`. They used to carry none, or antiforgery's `SAMEORIGIN` on a visitor's first page. Every policy counts, several joined by commas included, and the strictest decides; a report-only policy does not count. A partner site named in `frame-ancestors` can no longer frame the app in a browser that knows only `X-Frame-Options`. An app that wants another value sends its own `X-Frame-Options`, which Netjes keeps. An app whose code stores antiforgery tokens before a page renders (`IAntiforgery.GetAndStoreTokens` in a loader or a middleware) still gets antiforgery's `SAMEORIGIN` on a first visit: set `AntiforgeryOptions.SuppressXFrameOptionsHeader = true` to get the one the policy implies ([ADR 0030](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0030-security-headers-beyond-documents.md)).
- In production, a sidecar script of the app's own (`Netjes:SidecarScript`) must answer `GET /health`, with any status and without reading a request body. Netjes now sends that request to a Node process that has answered no render for 5 seconds, and kills and restarts a process that sends nothing back within `RenderTimeout`, never less than 5 seconds. The sidecar Netjes ships has always answered it, so an app that uses it has nothing to change. A script that exits on the request, as one that reads every request as a render can, is restarted at every ping, and `Netjes.Sidecar.NodeSidecar` logs a warning that names `GET /health` and `Netjes:SidecarScript`.
- `CachePage` keeps its own copy of its tags, for the page's cache entries as for its `CachedPageMetadata`, so the two agree: changing the array after the call used to change the tags the entries got, and no longer does. An app that did that passes the tags it means to `CachePage` instead.
- React no longer compares the text directly in `<body>`, outside any element or `<Suspense>` boundary, in production as in development, since `<body>` now carries `suppressHydrationWarning` (see the entry on attributes under Fixed, [ADR 0026](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0026-netjes-html-and-body-skip-reacts-attribute-check.md)). When such text differs between the server and the browser, React used to report it (#418 in production) and render the page again in the browser; now it reports nothing, and the page keeps the server's text until that text changes. An app that renders text there that can differ, such as a time next to a layout's `{children}`, puts it in an element.
- `netjes --help` links the CLI reference at the release tag of the installed version (`https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/v<version>/docs/reference/cli.md`), not the page on `main`, which can describe commands and options that version does not have. The READMEs on npm and NuGet do the same from this release on: the release moves their links to the docs from `main` to its tag in the packages it publishes, and they link the security policy at `https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/security/policy`, which always shows the current one ([ADR 0032](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0032-release-links-package-readmes-to-its-tag.md)). Apps have nothing to change.
- When a client navigation shows another page, the focus starts over at the top of the document, as after a page load: the next Tab goes to the first element that takes the focus. It used to stay on the link that was followed when that link was in a layout, and to fall back to `body` when the link went with the old page. The element a `#fragment` names now takes the focus, on the page on screen and on another, with `tabindex="-1"` until it loses the focus again when it takes none of its own; the router used to scroll to it only. The focus stays where it is after a navigation that changes only the query, `router.refresh()`, a form post that stays on its page and a modal that an intercepting route opens or Back closes; where the new page (`autoFocus`), the user or the app's code moved it while the navigation ran, a link's own `onClick` and a form's own `onSubmit` included; on a `scroll={false}` link that still has it; and in a field the user types into, such as a search box in a layout that navigates as the user types. No focus call scrolls, so the scroll position after a navigation is as before, the one Back restores included ([Focus and announcements](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/routing.md#focus-and-announcements), [ADR 0033](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0033-client-navigations-announce-the-page-and-start-the-focus-over.md)). Remove code of the app's own that focuses a fragment's element after a navigation. An end-to-end test that types right after a navigation to another page without focusing a field first now types into `body`: focus the field, as `locator.fill()` does. If a menu of the app closes in an effect after a navigation, let it give the focus back to its button only while the focus is still inside the menu; otherwise the button takes the focus from the top of the new page. Keyboard users now Tab through the header again after each navigation, so add a skip link (see Added). The promises of `router.push`, `router.replace` and `router.refresh()` resolve when they did before, once the router has handed the page to React, which can be before React shows it, as the docs now say ([ADR 0034](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0034-navigation-promises-resolve-when-react-has-the-page.md)): code that needs the new page runs in an effect.
- In the browser, zod now parses without compiled code. The client entry sets zod's `jitless` setting before any of the app's modules run, in every browser, with or without a Content-Security-Policy, and for every zod object schema made in the page: page and layout props, `api[...].response.parse(...)`, and the app's own search-param and form schemas ([zod in the browser](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/security.md#zod-in-the-browser), [ADR 0036](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0036-zod-runs-without-compiled-parsers-in-the-browser.md)). Parsing many objects with one schema is slower: a list of 1,000 small objects takes about 0.5 ms, against about 0.09 ms with compiled parsers. A new schema's first parse of one object, such as a page's props, is faster. Server rendering in the Node sidecar and the app's Vitest tests keep the compiled parsers, and Netjes has no setting to keep them in the browser. zod reads the setting from version 4.4.0 on, so an app on zod 4.0 to 4.3 upgrades zod to 4.4.0 or newer; an app made with `netjes new` asks for `^4.6.7` already. An app's own call of `z.compile(schema)` still makes a function from a string.
- A `GET` or `HEAD` for a page in another case of the literal segments its file names now answers 308 with the file's spelling: `/About` and `/ABOUT` go to `/about` for `app/about/page.tsx`, `/About/` to `/about/`, and `/ROBOTS.TXT` and `/Sitemap.xml` to `/robots.txt` and `/sitemap.xml`. A client navigation to such a URL gets a redirect payload, and the router shows the file's spelling. These URLs used to render the page as sent, so each was a page of its own to crawlers and to the output cache, and `<Link>` marked no link current on it. Only the literal segments change: route values (`/Blog/Hello` goes to `/blog/Hello`), the query string and the base path keep their case and encoding, and a trailing slash stays unless `TrailingSlash` is `Never`. Only the URL the client sent is redirected, and only to a page's spelling: a request that a rewrite or a re-execution changed (`UseRewriter`, `UseStatusCodePagesWithReExecute`, `UseExceptionHandler`, the page rendered for a failed form post) is answered as before, and so are requests with other methods, the app's own endpoints, the not-found page and every request on TestServer, which passes on no request target, so `WebApplicationFactory` tests still get the page. The redirect comes at the end of `UseNetjes()`, ahead of authentication and the output cache, so the output cache stores no other case that a browser sends. A request target that browsers do not send, with `.` or `..` segments (`/./About`) or in absolute form (`GET http://example.com/About`), is answered, and can be stored, as before. Browsers keep a 308: after a folder is renamed to another case, a visitor whose browser followed the old redirect is sent round in a loop until the browser forgets it. An app that serves pages at mixed-case URLs on purpose sets `NetjesOptions.RedirectLiteralCase = false` (`Netjes:RedirectLiteralCase=false`), which answers every case as before. A loader that redirected to its own spelling of a literal can drop that check. A test on Kestrel or in a browser that requests a page in another case now gets the 308 ([One URL per page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/routing.md#one-url-per-page), [ADR 0039](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0039-a-page-url-has-one-spelling.md)).
- `isRouteHref`, and with it the generated `isHref()` and `Href` schema, refuses a URL that holds an ASCII control character (U+0000 to U+001F, or U+007F) or that starts or ends with a space. Browsers drop tabs and newlines anywhere in a URL, and control characters and spaces at either end, so `/\t/evil.example`, which `isRouteHref` took for a path where a root catch-all or two dynamic segments match, went to `evil.example`. A URL from data that holds such a character now fails `Href.parse`, and `isHref` returns false for it: trim it, or take the character out, before it is checked. Other URLs are checked as before.
- Netjes has new public types named `Href`, `HrefJsonConverter` and `TrailingSlash`, in the `Netjes` namespace, which the package's build targets import into every C# file of an app with implicit usings. A file that also imports another namespace with a type of one of these names, the app's own or a library's, now gets error CS0104 (an ambiguous reference) where it names that type: qualify the name, or give one of the two an alias (`using CmsHref = MyCms.Href;`). A type of that name in the namespace the file declares, or in one around it, is not ambiguous and is still the one the file gets.
- The docs index ([`docs/README.md`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/README.md)) lists the guides in the order an app is built, in four groups with a heading each: Build (Routing, Data loading, Actions and forms), Render (Rendering and streaming, Caching, Images), Publish (Metadata, Static export, Redirects, rewrites and headers) and Run (Security, Testing, Deployment, Coding agents). They were one list, in which Images came after Metadata, Deployment before Testing and Redirects, rewrites and headers after Testing. `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` list the guides in the new order, and so do the documentation table in the README, the React API reference and the agent skill's pointer to the guides. The guides themselves are unchanged, and apps have nothing to do. A site or a tool that builds a navigation from the index now finds four `###` headings under `## Guides`, each followed by its guides as bullets, where the bullets sat directly under `## Guides`.
- An error that only the router's top-level boundary catches, with no segment's `error.tsx` above it, now reaches the root `app/error.tsx` as it was thrown: with its own class and stack, a `ServerActionError`'s status, and no `status` for any other error. It used to be a new Error with status 500. An error page that shows the status should show `error.status ?? 500`, as the examples do.
