A thrown string keeps its text there and on the built-in error page, which used to show "Something went wrong" for it; the built-in page still says 500.
- `error.stack` is undefined in the browser for an error page the server rendered without a stack (error details off). It used to be the stack of the client code that built the error.
- A `Page.Defer` value whose failure the server withholds (error details off) now travels as an empty error string, where it was "Something went wrong": in its `self.__netjes_d(id, null, "")` script, in the documents `netjes export` writes as in streamed ones, in the `error` of its NDJSON line, and in `ISsrRenderer.ResolveAsync` and the sidecar's `/resolve`. The browser still rejects the value with the message "Something went wrong", now with `withheld` true. A custom `ISsrRenderer` passes an empty error on as it is, and a test that read "Something went wrong" from a document or a stream expects `""`. With error details on, an exception whose message is empty reads as withheld too.
- A `Page.Defer` value whose task was cancelled now fails with "The value was cancelled" in every environment, where it was "Something went wrong".
- An external `<Script strategy="beforeInteractive">` is no longer an async script in the head, which ran whenever it arrived, in no order. The server now preloads it and writes an inert entry where the component stands; once the shell is parsed, the client entry runs these scripts one after the other, in the order they stand in the document, with the page's nonce, and the page's modules run and the page hydrates once each of them has loaded or failed. They do not hold up rendering, but a slow host now delays the page's interactivity: give a script the page does not need before then `strategy="afterInteractive"`. The script keeps its `id` and attributes. One the browser does not run, with `noModule` or a `type` that is neither JavaScript nor `module` (a consent manager's `text/plain`), is added to the head but neither preloaded nor waited for. A page with any `beforeInteractive` script, inline or external, runs its own modules once the shell is parsed, instead of while the rest of the shell arrives, and its head has a `<meta name="netjes-before-interactive">`; a test that snapshots the head sees it. A component that mounts in the browser (after a client navigation, when no sidecar was ready, or in a `createTestApp()` test) adds its script after it mounts, as `afterInteractive` does, and one the server's document already ran is not added again. Keep these scripts outside Suspense boundaries that may still wait when the shell goes out: there an external one runs when its part of the page hydrates. In development Netjes warns about `async`, `defer` and `type="module"` on such a script ([code that runs before the first paint](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/metadata.md#code-that-runs-before-the-first-paint), [ADR 0044](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0044-before-interactive-scripts-run-before-the-pages-code.md)).
- The export of an app that maps `MapSitemap` or `MapRobotsTxt` and falls back to a localhost site URL when none is configured, as the docs' example does, now publishes links to localhost in `sitemap.xml` and `robots.txt`. The export writes them and logs a warning for each in `Netjes.Export.StaticExportService`, and its exit code is unchanged. Set the static host's URL for the export, such as `SiteUrl=https://www.example.com npx netjes export` when the app reads `app.Configuration["SiteUrl"]`, or leave both files out with `.ExcludeFromExport()` ([static export](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/static-export.md#sitemap-and-robotstxt)).
- `netjes export` fails before it writes anything when a `robots.txt` or `sitemap.xml` in `public/`, or one a Vite plugin writes into the client build, has the path of `MapRobotsTxt` or `MapSitemap`: the app serves that file ahead of routing, so the endpoint never answered, and the export used to copy the file. Remove the file or the Map call, or keep the file and add `.ExcludeFromExport()` to the Map call. The export also fails on a `MapSitemap` or `MapRobotsTxt` mapped in a route group with route parameters, such as `/{lang}`, since it writes each one once: add `.ExcludeFromExport()` to the call. A page that needs a folder where the export writes a file, such as a page at `/404.html`, also fails the export now, naming both. The export's last line now reads `Exported N pages and M files to <dir>` ([static export](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/static-export.md#sitemap-and-robotstxt)).

### Fixed

- `<Link>` sets `aria-current="page"` only on a link to the page on screen ([ADR 0024](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0024-link-marks-the-current-page-by-path-and-query.md)). It used to compare the link's path alone, byte for byte. Now a link with a `#` (`/#features`, `#top`) is never marked; a link with a query is marked only while the page has the same values for every parameter the link names, in any order (`/search?q=other` is no longer marked on `/search?q=cache`); `/x` and `/x/` count as one page; and a link whose `href` already starts with the base path is marked on its page. Parameters a link leaves out still do not count, so a link that names fewer of them than the page is still marked, such as an "All" filter (`/blog`) on `/blog?tag=react`, or a `?page=2` link that drops the page's filter: set `aria-current` on such links yourself (`aria-current={undefined}` leaves it off). Check how filter and tab bars that style `aria-current` look, since which of their links are marked can change. Links with neither a `#` nor a query are marked as before, and now also when the page's path differs from theirs by a trailing slash. The [routing guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/routing.md#the-current-section) shows how to mark a section link, such as Docs on every page under `/docs`, with `aria-current="true"`.
- A `title.default` on a layout below the root, or on a page, now goes through the nearest `title.template` of the layouts above it, as [the metadata guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/metadata.md#titles) says and Next.js does. It skipped the templates before: below a root template of `'%s · Site'`, a docs layout's `default: 'Docs'` gave the title `Docs`, and it now gives `Docs · Site` (never `Docs · Docs · Site`, since a default does not go through the template next to it). A page's `title: { default: 'Intro' }` goes through the template in the same way, and so do the Open Graph and Twitter titles that fall back to the page's title. An app whose titles change this way and that wants them bare sets `title: { absolute: 'Docs' }` on that layout or page, which skips every template. A `default` on the root layout, and a title with no template above it, are unchanged.
- In development, a script that sets an attribute on `<html>` or `<body>` before the page hydrates, such as a theme script, a browser extension or a translator, no longer makes React log a hydration error. Netjes renders both elements and an app's layout cannot reach them, so both now carry `suppressHydrationWarning`, which ends React's attribute check for their own attributes ([ADR 0026](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0026-netjes-html-and-body-skip-reacts-attribute-check.md)). The markup the server sends is the same, and React does not check attributes in production. A mismatch in the head, or in any element in the body, is still reported, apart from the text of the development `<style data-vite-dev-id>` elements (see the entry on development CSS below); a different `lang` on `<html>` is not. The prop also changes what React compares in production: see the entry on text directly in `<body>` under Changed.
- `/robots.txt`, `/sitemap.xml`, `/_netjes/image` and the locale redirect at `/` answer `HEAD` as they answer `GET`, with the same status and headers and without the body. They answered `GET` only, so a `HEAD`, which crawlers and link checkers send, went to whatever else matched the URL: for `/robots.txt` and `/sitemap.xml` an empty 404, or a dynamic page at the root (`app/[lang]/page.tsx` answered with its not-found page); for the image endpoint and the redirect, the not-found page. An app that answered such a `HEAD` itself, with an endpoint of its own for `HEAD` at one of these URLs next to Netjes's, now gets 500 for it: both endpoints take `HEAD` there, with the same order and route precedence, so ASP.NET Core cannot choose between them (`AmbiguousMatchException`). Remove that endpoint; other apps have nothing to change. `netjes routes` now lists a `HEAD` row next to the `GET` row of each. Under output caching, a `HEAD` for an image is stored apart from the `GET`, so the first `HEAD` processes the image once more. `/_netjes/antiforgery` still answers `GET` only, and so does an endpoint an app maps with `MapGet`: map it with `MapMethods(pattern, [HttpMethods.Get, HttpMethods.Head], handler)` to answer `HEAD` too ([HEAD requests](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/routing.md#head-requests)).
- A Node process that stops answering without exiting (stuck in a loop, deadlocked, stopped by a signal) is now restarted, as one that crashed is. It used to stay ready: every server-rendered page waited out `RenderTimeout`, and its error page as long again, before a plain 500 went out; `/healthz` answered Healthy; and the client-rendered fallback never stepped in. In production Netjes now pings a process that has answered no render for 5 seconds, on a loopback connection of its own rather than through the HTTP client, so a ping records no HTTP client span or metric, and kills and restarts a process that sends nothing back within `RenderTimeout`, never less than 5 seconds ([ADR 0031](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0031-a-sidecar-that-stops-answering-is-restarted.md)). From the moment the process is taken out, `/healthz` reports Unhealthy (Degraded while other processes are ready), documents get the client-rendered fallback while no process is ready, and `Netjes.Sidecar.NodeSidecar` logs an error. Development is unchanged. Apps have nothing to do: a restart policy that acts when the container exits, as the template's `restart: always` does, is all a host needs. A synchronous render that holds a process for longer than `RenderTimeout`, which fails at that time limit as before, can now get the process restarted as well.
- `netjes export` with an output folder outside the app now exits 1 at once, with one line that names the folder and the app, and builds nothing. It used to build first (the types, both Vite bundles and a Release compile) and start the app with its Node sidecar, and only then did the app refuse the folder. The CLI compares the paths as .NET does, ignoring letter case on macOS and Windows. On macOS and Linux it takes the app's folder by its real path, with any symlink resolved, as the app sees its own folder, and resolves a relative output folder against it, with or without `--no-build`, so `out` now exports when `--cwd` names the app through a symlink, where the app used to refuse it. `netjes export --no-build` still leaves the check to the app, against `Netjes:Root`. A script that passes a folder outside the app now fails before the build: pass a folder inside the app, such as `out`.
- `netjes export` takes an output folder whose name starts with two dots, such as `..site`, as a folder inside the app; it used to refuse it as outside the app. For the same reason, such a folder inside one the app needs, such as `app/..site`, was not seen to overlap it, and the export wrote into it: it is now refused like any other folder there. `netjes new ..shop` now shows the new app's folder as `..shop` rather than by its absolute path. Apps have nothing to change.
- In development, the CSS that the sidecar inlines into a document, as `<style data-vite-dev-id>` elements, is now the browser's build of each file, made by Vite's client environment, and no longer a second build from Vite's SSR environment. When the two differed, Vite's client replaced the text before the page hydrated, and React logged a hydration error for the `<style>` ("A tree hydrated but some attributes of the server rendered HTML didn't match the client properties"). With `css.devSourcemap` on, that happened on every page that imports CSS, since only the browser's build carries the source map comment; it could also happen with a plugin that builds a file differently in each environment, as Tailwind CSS can after many edits. React also no longer compares the text of these elements, which Vite's client owns once it runs, so a file edited between the render and the import logs nothing either ([ADR 0035](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0035-development-styles-are-inlined-from-the-client-build.md)). Apps have nothing to change, and production, which links the built stylesheets, is unchanged. Should a Vite version write the module it serves for a CSS file in development in a form Netjes does not read, the sidecar inlines the SSR build as before and logs one warning, which names the first such file.
- A page under a Content-Security-Policy whose `script-src` leaves out `'unsafe-eval'`, such as the nonce-based and hash-based policies the [security guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/security.md#content-security-policy) shows, or that has no `script-src` and a `default-src` without it, no longer reports a violation as it loads. The first time a page module made a zod object schema, zod tested whether it may make a function from a string, the policy refused it, and the browser reported a `script-src` violation (blocked URI `eval`) on every document: a `securitypolicyviolation` event, and a report to the policy's `report-uri` or `report-to` endpoint when it has one. zod caught the error and the page worked. Chromium logged nothing to the console when the policy had a `script-src`; when the policy left scripts to `default-src`, Chromium logged one error on every document, which read in full "Note that 'script-src' was not explicitly set, so 'default-src' is used as a fallback." With zod 4.4.0 or newer, zod no longer makes that test in the browser, since it parses there without compiled code (under Changed). An app that turned zod's compiled parsers off itself to avoid the report, for example with a build hook that sets `jitless` in the chunks that hold zod, can remove that.
- A container of the template's production image now stops when the app crashes. The image started `dotnet <App>.dll` as the container's first process, PID 1, and the kernel ignores a signal that a container's PID 1 has no handler for, so when .NET aborted the process after a crash (an exception that nothing catches, `Environment.FailFast`, a stack overflow), the process did not end. On arm64 the thread that crashed spun at 100% of a CPU and the process never exited, so the container stayed up and `restart: always` never restarted it. After a crash at startup the container was unhealthy, but after a later one, such as on a thread of the app's own, the rest of the app kept serving and its health check still passed. On x86-64 under emulation it exited after a few seconds, with code 139 instead of 134. The image now starts the app with `tini -s -- dotnet <App>.dll`: tini, from Ubuntu's package, is PID 1 and passes the signals it gets on to the app, so `docker stop` still stops it at once, and it exits with the app's code, so a crash ends the container with 134 ([a crash in a container](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/deployment.md#a-crash-in-a-container), [ADR 0042](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0042-the-apps-image-runs-an-init-as-pid-1.md)). Netjes's own startup failures still exit with code 1, and monitoring that expects 1 for every failed start now sees 134 for the other exceptions. Building the image needs Ubuntu's package archive for the new `tini` stage. An app made before this release copies three things from the template's `Dockerfile`: the `tini` stage (`FROM ${SDK_IMAGE} AS tini` and its `RUN apt-get ...` line), `COPY --from=tini /usr/bin/tini-static /usr/bin/tini` in the `production` stage, and the `ENTRYPOINT`, with its own dll name; or it runs its container under an init of the host's, such as `docker run --init` or `init: true` in Compose. The Blog's and TaskBoard's images run under tini as well.
- `llms.txt` lists `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `SECURITY.md`, which the docs index links. The generator named neither, and it listed a document it was not told about only when the document is under `docs/`, so both were missing from `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt`. Both are under Optional, after the roadmap. `CONTRIBUTING.md` is in `llms.txt` only, marked as not in `llms-full.txt` as the architecture page is, and `SECURITY.md` is in `llms-full.txt` too: an agent that reads that file now also reads the security policy, with the address it gives for reporting a vulnerability. The generator now also lists any Markdown file in the repository that the docs index links and no entry names, under More, after the documents under `docs/` and in the order the index links them, so a page the index shows readers cannot be left out again; decision records stay out. Apps have nothing to change.
- Inline `<Script strategy="beforeInteractive">` code runs before the first paint of what follows it. The server writes it where the component stands, with the page's nonce, and the browser's parser runs it there, after the stylesheets before it have loaded; it used to be added to the body after hydration, as `afterInteractive` code is, so a theme script set `<html>`'s attributes after the page had been painted. The code is written as given, except that the `s` of `<script` and `</script`, in any case, becomes `\u0073` (`\u0053` for `S`), as React writes its own scripts, so the code cannot end its element. Under a hash-based policy, list the hash of the code as the document carries it, which is also the text a client render adds: `inlineScriptHashes(await renderDocument(...))` from `netjes/testing` now lists it, so a test that compares a page's inline scripts with `CSP_SCRIPT_HASHES` expects it too, as the Blog example's `app/document.test.ts` does. Inline code runs before any external `beforeInteractive` script, so it cannot use what one defines ([code that runs before the first paint](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/metadata.md#code-that-runs-before-the-first-paint)).
- `onLoad` and `onError` of an external `<Script strategy="beforeInteractive">` are called once the script has loaded or failed. They were never called.

## [0.0.2] - 2026-11-03

### Fixed

- A page could show twice. When the client entry came from the browser's cache, it could hydrate a streamed document before the shell had been parsed; React reported a hydration error (#418), rendered the page itself, and the rest of the server's HTML followed it. The client entry now waits for the end of the shell ([ADR 0022](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0022-hydrate-once-the-shell-is-parsed.md)). Every server-rendered document ends its body with an empty `<template id="__NETJES_SHELL_END__">`. Apps have nothing to change, but a stylesheet that targets the body's last child now matches it.

## [0.0.1] - 2026-10-30

Initial release.

### Added

- **Routing.** Pages in `app/` with the Next.js App Router conventions: `page`, `layout`, `template`, `loading`, `error`, `not-found`, `forbidden`, `unauthorized` and `global-error` files, route groups, private folders, dynamic, catch-all and optional catch-all segments, and parallel and intercepting routes. Each page is an ASP.NET Core endpoint, so the matcher, `RequireAuthorization()` and other endpoint conventions apply. Route warnings at startup and in `netjes routes` for loader parameters that miss a route value, for pages that match the same URLs, and for form inputs that refuse a post without a checkbox.
- **Client router.** `<Link>` with prefetching, `useRouter`, `usePathname`, `useSearchParams` and `useParams` with optional schemas, `useSelectedLayoutSegment(s)`, `useNavigation`, scroll restoration, and back and forward from memory for the last 50 pages. Base paths (`UsePathBase` with `netjes({ basePath })`) and locale routing on a `[lang]` segment (`AddNetjesLocalization`, `useLocale`).
- **Data loading.** C# page loaders (`MapPageLoader`) and layout loaders (`MapLayoutLoader`) that bind like minimal API handlers and return `Page.Props`, `NotFound`, `Forbidden`, `Unauthorized`, `Redirect` or `LocalRedirect`. Layout loaders are skipped on navigations within their section, keyed by signed segment keys. Shared props for every page (`UseSharedProps`), public configuration read at runtime (`Netjes:PublicConfig`, `usePublicConfig`), and a built-in TanStack Query client seeded from loaders with `.WithQuery`.
- **Generated types.** `generated/netjes.ts`, written from the app's System.Text.Json contracts: zod schemas for page and layout props, shared props, JSON endpoints and page action forms, typed server action references, typed routes (`route()`, `Href`), and `definePage` and `defineLayout` to parse props with them. `netjes generate --check` for CI.
- **Server actions and forms.** `MapAction` endpoints with typed references, `useAction` and `<Form>`, DataAnnotations and `IValidatableObject` validation, `ServerAction.Ok`, `Invalid`, `Redirect`, `Forbidden` and `NotFound`, revalidation of cached pages and refreshes, TanStack Query updates, and page actions (`MapPageAction`), whose inputs are validated the same way, with the errors in `usePageActionState`. Forms post without JavaScript and come back with their errors and the declared fields' values. Antiforgery and same-origin checks on every action, a 1 MB body limit for server actions, and a refresh of the router's memory and query cache, in every tab of the app, when an action signs someone in or out.
- **Rendering.** Server rendering in a pool of supervised Node processes (`SidecarProcesses`), restarted with backoff and reported by a health check. Streamed documents with `loading.tsx` and Suspense, `Page.Defer` for slow values (with an overload that runs the work in its own DI scope), ready boundaries written in place, complete documents for crawlers, and a document the browser renders itself when no Node process is ready in production. `dynamic()`, `clientOnly()`, error pages and built-in fallbacks.
- **Caching.** `.CachePage(duration, tags)` on ASP.NET Core output caching, with Netjes's keys under any output-cache policy; revalidation by tag or path from actions or through `IPageCache`; draft mode (`IDraftMode`, `useDraftMode`) that bypasses the cache. Pages that are not cached go out `no-store`.
- **Metadata, images and scripts.** The Metadata API on pages and layouts and `PageMetadata` from C#, `MapSitemap` and `MapRobotsTxt`, `<Script>` with three loading strategies, and `<Image>` with the `/_netjes/image` endpoint: configured widths and qualities, allow-listed remote hosts, bounded concurrency, and a pluggable `IImageProcessor`. `Netjes.Images.SkiaSharp` resizes and encodes WebP.
- **Static export.** `netjes export` writes every page as a complete HTML document, with `.StaticParams(...)` for dynamic pages and `.ExcludeFromExport()`, and refuses pages that need a server.
- **Security.** `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Referrer-Policy` and a same-origin framing policy on every document, an opt-in Content-Security-Policy with per-request nonces or hashes, redirects limited to relative and http(s) URLs, form fields that look like secrets never handed back, and a token on every request to the Node processes.
- **Operations.** The `Netjes` ActivitySource and Meter for OpenTelemetry (loader, action, render and sidecar spans and durations, web vitals with `netjes/vitals`), a health check, and support for several instances sharing an output-cache store.
- **Testing.** Vitest defaults in the Vite plugin and `createTestApp()` from `netjes/testing`, with a fake router, seeded queries and fake server actions.
- **Tooling.** The `netjes` command: `new`, `dev`, `build`, `start`, `generate`, `routes`, `export`, `info` and `agents`. An app template with a C# loader, a validated server action, component tests, Tailwind CSS and Docker files for development and production. `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and a Netjes skill for coding agents in new apps, and `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` for the docs. The npm package ships compiled ES modules with type declarations.

# Roadmap

The work in progress, what comes next, what is planned without a date, and what is left out by design. Nothing here is a promise: plans change as people use Netjes and report what they need. To ask for something, or to say that an item matters to you, open a discussion or an issue on GitHub.

## Now

- **The 0.0.1 release.** The packages `netjes` on npm and `Netjes` and `Netjes.Images.SkiaSharp` on NuGet, released together under one version, with the documentation, `llms.txt` and the app template.

## Next

- **Apps without Node in production.** An option to render every page in the browser, from the client-rendered document Netjes already serves while no Node process is ready, so an app runs on .NET alone. Loaders, actions, typed props and client navigation keep working. What goes is what server rendering gives: HTML for crawlers and link previews, the metadata in that HTML, forms that work before the JavaScript loads, and caching of documents (a client-rendered document goes out `no-store`; data payloads can still be cached). It revisits [ADR 0001](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0001-react-renders-in-node-sidecars.md), which chose server rendering, so it starts with a new decision record.
- **Instant loading.** On a client navigation, show the target's `loading.tsx` at once inside the layouts it shares with the current page, then stream in the layout loaders' props and the page as they are ready, instead of waiting for the whole payload.
- **Caching depth.** Stale-while-revalidate for cached pages, cache profiles, tags added by a loader at render time, revalidation by route pattern or layout, and a cached shell that is filled for an anonymous visitor, for pages with a part that differs per visitor.
- **Metadata and images.** The metadata file conventions in `app/` (`icon`, `apple-icon`, `opengraph-image`, `twitter-image`, `manifest`), generated Open Graph images, richer sitemaps and `robots.txt`, `metadataBase` and `viewport`, and more of `<Image>`: `fill`, blur placeholders and static imports.
- **Client navigation in static exports.** Write each page's payload next to its HTML, so exported sites navigate without full page loads, files written to match `TrailingSlash` (and a `TrailingSlash.Always`), and images resized at export time.
- **Bundle size.** Smaller first-load JavaScript: generated schemas split per route and free of side effects, so bundlers can drop what a page does not use, and `dynamic()` chunks preloaded from the build manifest.
- **Error handling.** An id for each server error, logged with the exception and shown to the user, a way to retry the failed segment from `error.tsx`, and a global error boundary in the browser.
- **Internationalisation.** Redirects from paths without a locale, `hreflang` alternates from the supported cultures, and optional domains per locale.
- **Operations.** Streamed responses that proxies do not buffer, an asset prefix for serving the client build from a CDN, a deployment id, and letting renders in progress finish when a Node process is stopped.

## Later

- Partial prerendering: a cached HTML shell, resumed by React with the parts that differ per request.
- valibot as an alternative to zod in the generated file.
- Navigations that keep what an unmatched parallel-route slot showed, as Next.js does after a soft navigation.
- Back and Forward that give the focus back to the element that had it when the user left the entry, found again in the page that renders anew ([ADR 0033](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0033-client-navigations-announce-the-page-and-start-the-focus-over.md)).
- A `__Host-` antiforgery cookie by default. It is an opt-in today for apps served only over HTTPS: as a default it would break plain-HTTP development and `UsePathBase`.
- AVIF output for `<Image>`, from a second image processor.
- Typegen edge cases: item nullability for collection subclasses (`class Tags : List<string?>`), `UnknownDerivedTypeHandling.FallBackToBaseType` in discriminated unions, and read semantics (defaulted properties optional, computed ones left out) for JSON endpoint request schemas, as server action inputs have.
- Agent files that follow the installed version. `netjes new` and `netjes agents` copy the `netjes` skill and `AGENTS.md` into an app with links to the docs on `main`, which can describe a newer version than the app has. Linking the installed version's tag instead needs a way to bring those copies up to date when the app upgrades Netjes; today that is a step by hand ([Coding agents](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/coding-agents.md#after-upgrading-netjes)).

## Not planned

Netjes leaves these out by design. Taking one up would need a new decision record that supersedes the one named.

- React Server Components. C# loaders do their job: data comes from C# as props, and every component ships to the browser ([ADR 0010](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0010-app-router-with-csharp-layout-loaders.md)).
- The pages router, and its hooks for code moving from `pages/`: `useRouter().query`, `asPath`, router events and shallow routing ([ADR 0010](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0010-app-router-with-csharp-layout-loaders.md)).
- Serverless and edge hosts. Pages render in long-lived Node processes next to the .NET app ([ADR 0001](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0001-react-renders-in-node-sidecars.md)).

<!-- Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/SECURITY.md -->

# Security policy

## Supported versions

Netjes is at 0.0.x. Only the latest 0.0.x release gets security fixes; upgrade to it before reporting something you found in an older one. This covers the `netjes` npm package and the `Netjes` and `Netjes.Images.SkiaSharp` NuGet packages, which are released at the same version.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Please do not open a public issue, pull request or discussion for a vulnerability.

1. **Preferred:** use GitHub's private vulnerability reporting: <https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/security/advisories/new>.
2. **Fallback:** e-mail dennis.verhoeven@proton.me.

Please include:

- the Netjes version (npm and NuGet), the .NET SDK and Node.js versions, and the operating system;
- what you found and what an attacker gains from it;
- the smallest app or request sequence that shows it (a repository, a test, or `curl` commands);
- whether it needs a particular configuration, such as output caching, a CSP, or a reverse proxy;
- anything you already know about a fix.

## What to expect

- An acknowledgement within a week.
- A first assessment, and questions if the report is unclear, after that.
- Coordinated disclosure: we agree on a date with you, fix the issue in a new release, publish a GitHub security advisory, and credit you unless you prefer not to be named.

Netjes is maintained by one person in spare time, so the time to a fix depends on the severity and the size of the change; reports about the defaults and about code that guards a trust boundary come first.

## Security model

What Netjes does by default, so you can tell a bug from a documented limit. The [security guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/security.md), the [options reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/reference/options.md) and [docs/architecture.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/architecture.md) have the details and the settings.

- **Server actions and page actions** require a valid antiforgery token and a same-origin request (`Origin` or `Sec-Fetch-Site`); `Netjes:AllowedActionOrigins` adds origins. A page action can opt out with `.DisableAntiforgery()`, which turns off both checks (for a provider that posts back from its own site); on a server action it turns off the token check only. A failed form never hands back fields that look like secrets (`Netjes:PrivateFormFields`).
- **Server action bodies** are limited to 1 MB by default (`Netjes:ActionBodySizeLimit`). Page actions keep the server's own request size limit.
- **Layout segment keys**, which let the client router skip layouts it already has, are signed with HMAC-SHA256 using `Netjes:SegmentKeySecret` (at least 32 bytes, random per process unless you set one), so a client cannot make up a key for a segment it was not given.
- **The Node sidecar** listens on the loopback interface only, and every request to it must carry a random token generated when the app starts; it does not start without one.
- **The output cache** (`CachePage`, and the same rules under any output-cache policy) keys page entries on the scheme, the host, the path and query string as sent, whether the response is a document or a client payload, the layouts the client holds, and the client build. It does not store responses it cannot safely share: signed-in users, requests with an `Authorization` header, responses that set cookies, non-200 statuses, and documents carrying a CSP nonce. A cached page that reads request cookies is still stored and served to everyone; Netjes logs a warning. Cached pages carry no antiforgery token; forms fetch one first.
- **The image endpoint** accepts only configured widths and qualities, reads local images from `public/` only, fetches remote images only from hosts you list (https only, listed ports, public addresses only, no redirects followed, with a timeout), caps the source size and, with the SkiaSharp processor, the pixel count, bounds concurrency and queue length, and serves SVG only when you turn it on, sandboxed.
- **Security headers:** `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` on every response that passes through `UseNetjes()` (documents, client payloads, static files, the app's own endpoints and answers from the output cache, but not a response that middleware registered before it writes itself), and on rendered documents `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin` and a same-origin framing policy, each unless your app sets that header itself. With `frame-ancestors` in the Content-Security-Policy that goes out, documents carry the `X-Frame-Options` it implies instead: `SAMEORIGIN` when the list holds `'self'`, `*` or a scheme source, `DENY` otherwise. Netjes sends every page response the output cache does not store, for visitors and signed-in users alike, with `Cache-Control: no-store, private` unless the page sets its own (the response that sets the antiforgery cookie carries ASP.NET Core's `no-cache, no-store` instead).
- **Content Security Policy** is opt-in: set `Netjes:ContentSecurityPolicy` with `{nonce}` and Netjes sends the header and puts a per-request nonce on the scripts and styles it renders. Netjes does not send a CSP until you configure one. The policy goes out as written, in Development too, and Netjes logs a warning, once per policy, when the policy on a document, its own or the app's, refuses what the document needs.
- **Endpoint routes:** the generated file names the route of each of the app's endpoints with an `endpointUrl` key, one mapped only in Development included, and these routes reach the browser once a component calls `endpointUrl`. A route in the file is no easier to reach than one outside it: authorization stays on the endpoint ([security guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/security.md#errors-and-configuration)).
- **Redirects and static export:** `Page.Redirect` accepts relative and absolute http(s) URLs and rejects encoded schemes, so use `Page.LocalRedirect` for URLs taken from the request; static export does not follow redirects, and writes a redirect only when the page itself issued it and its target is site-relative or http(s). Netjes's own 308 from another spelling of a page's URL, or of `/robots.txt` and `/sitemap.xml` (`Netjes:RedirectLiteralCase`, on by default, and `Netjes:TrailingSlash` set to `Never`), goes only to a `GET` or `HEAD`, is built from the URL the client sent, and never sends a location that a browser could read as another site; a request whose location would be one is answered as sent instead.

Out of scope: vulnerabilities in your own loaders and actions, in a reverse proxy or CDN in front of the app, or in a dependency (report those upstream, and tell us if Netjes should pin or work around it).
